## Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation — Near-saturated Schnakenberg pattern: near-stationarity and grid/time convergence [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-biology/
Coverage: reading

Compare raw L1/L2/L∞ with a spatially independent cosine Fourier–Galerkin/Radau reference (K32/64/96, cubic projection M=4(K+1)>4K, analytic Jacobian). Separately check K and ODE-tolerance sensitivity. Measure time order against a separately implemented Radau integration of the SAME FD semidiscretization. Norms are per-species mean-absolute/RMS/maximum, then the worse species. Record source/sink balance, every-step positive concentrations, initially absent k≥5 (first allowed k6 here), and departure from linearization. Convergence norms and reference sensitivities are assessed at the fixed final time; intermediate snapshot errors are separate evolution diagnostics.
No corresponding reference-library card is registered. The execution-specific validation material above documents its reference values and acceptance checks.
Input and validation protocol history · Initial input

## Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-biology/#schnakenberg-pattern-assumptions
Coverage: reading

1D periodic x∈[0,2π), a=.1,b=.9,D=(.01,1). Common IC u=1+.08cos(2x)+.01cos(4x), v=.9−.03cos(2x)−.002cos(4x), restricted to a reflection-even, pi-periodic invariant subspace with a fixed origin.

## Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-biology/#schnakenberg-pattern-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Strang-compose exact half-step diffusion of the FD matrix, diagonalized by FFT with symbol −4sin²(πk/N)/dx², and a full implicit-midpoint reaction step solved by local2×2 Newton iterations. FFT does not change FD space into spectral space. Fail on nonconvergence/budget excess; never clip concentrations.
u_t=D_u u_{xx}+a-u+u^2v,\qquad v_t=D_v v_{xx}+b-u^2v\frac{d\langle u+v\rangle}{dt}=a+b-\langle u\rangle,\quad S_{n+1}-S_n=h(a+b-\langle\bar u\rangle)\lambda_{h,k}=-4\sin^2(\pi k/N)/\Delta x^2,\quad\Phi_h=e^{hDL_h/2}\,\Phi_{\rm midpoint}^{F}(h)\,e^{hDL_h/2}\|e\|_1=\max_s\frac1N\sum_j|e_{s,j}|,\quad\|e\|_2=\max_s\sqrt{\frac1N\sum_j e_{s,j}^2},\quad\|e\|_\infty=\max_{s,j}|e_{s,j}|

## Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-biology/#schnakenberg-pattern-validation
Coverage: reading

Compare raw L1/L2/L∞ with a spatially independent cosine Fourier–Galerkin/Radau reference (K32/64/96, cubic projection M=4(K+1)>4K, analytic Jacobian). Separately check K and ODE-tolerance sensitivity. Measure time order against a separately implemented Radau integration of the SAME FD semidiscretization. Norms are per-species mean-absolute/RMS/maximum, then the worse species. Record source/sink balance, every-step positive concentrations, initially absent k≥5 (first allowed k6 here), and departure from linearization. Convergence norms and reference sensitivities are assessed at the fixed final time; intermediate snapshot errors are separate evolution diagnostics.

## Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-biology/#schnakenberg-pattern-limits
Coverage: reading

A selected-symmetry1D educational model: no test of free noise-driven wavenumber selection, phase stability,2D spots or biological calibration. Not an original-paper reproduction. Implicit midpoint is A-stable but not L-stable or unconditionally positive; reactions do not conserve u+v. The initial coarse protocol failed; temporal resolution was strengthened while retaining every acceptance threshold and the failed record. No quantum calculations. Near-saturation refers to the reference90→100 test window; it proves no exact steady state, nonlinear stability or long-term attractor. A huge late linearized difference diagnoses failure of linearization, not numerical error.

## Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-biology/#schnakenberg-pattern-references
Coverage: reading

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
A. M. Turing (1952). The Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis · DOI: 10.1098/rstb.1952.0012
Review scope / review_level: original-paper-selected-sections
Checked the university-hosted original scan, sections 6–7 (printed pp.46–50), ring formulation/linearization and bibliography. Distinct from the adopted coefficients, finite-amplitude reference and mature shape.
J. Schnakenberg (1979). Simple chemical reaction systems with limit cycle behaviour · DOI: 10.1016/0022-5193(79)90042-0
Review scope / review_level: official-bibliography-and-publisher-indexed-abstract
Checked official PubMed bibliography/DOI and publisher-indexed abstract. Full text returned403. Historical source for the reaction family, not a claim to reproduce original coefficients or experiments.
G. Strang (1968). On the Construction and Comparison of Difference Schemes · DOI: 10.1137/0705041
Review scope / review_level: original-paper-selected-nonlinear-composition
Checked original pp.510–512 for half-step composition and nonlinear second-order construction. This does not guarantee positivity or accuracy at arbitrary steps in the adopted model.
E. Hairer (2010). Geometric Numerical Integration, Lecture2

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-biology/#schnakenberg-pattern-references
Coverage: reading

Review scope / review_level: author-lecture-selected-midpoint-and-splitting
Checked theorem3 and section5 of the author-hosted lecture for implicit-midpoint formula/order and symmetric splitting. Hamiltonian symplectic claims are not transferred to this chemical model.
The SciPy community (2024). SciPy1.14.1 solve_ivp and Radau reference
Review scope / review_level: official-versioned-api-specification
Checked official Radau IIA order5, local rtol/atol scaling, analytic Jacobians and termination status. ODE tolerances do not certify global continuum-PDE accuracy.

Follow the lower and upper branches of the same one-dimensional Bratu boundary-value problem; check tangents, the fold and spatial error against an independent analytic family.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Weighted pseudo-arclength continuation
Armijo-damped Newton
Centered spatial difference
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Use a unit tangent in h-sum(du squared)+d-lambda squared, a predictor and a tangent-hyperplane Newton corrector. A separate augmented system locates the fold and a normalized null vector. This case deliberately assembles sparse Jacobians.
Bratu nonlinear boundary-value problem
Dimensionless x in [0,1] with zero Dirichlet endpoints and 31/63/127 interior nodes. Take 80 fixed ds=0.1 steps from the zero solution. Correct both branches at lambda=2; lambda=4 is a deliberate discrete no-solution control. Pseudo-arclength is not physical time.

## Bratu fold continuation and Jacobian-free Newton-Krylov — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-bratu-continuation-jfnk/#bratu-fold-continuation-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Use a unit tangent in h-sum(du squared)+d-lambda squared, a predictor and a tangent-hyperplane Newton corrector. A separate augmented system locates the fold and a normalized null vector. This case deliberately assembles sparse Jacobians.

## Bratu fold continuation and Jacobian-free Newton-Krylov — Jacobian-free Newton–Krylov with analytic, central-FD and directional-AD products [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-bratu-continuation-jfnk/
Coverage: reading

Solve both Bratu branches with three Jv choices without assembling the nonlinear Jacobian; retain forcing, actual residuals and evaluation counts.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Jacobian-free Newton-Krylov
Restarted GMRES
Thomas tridiagonal elimination
Automatic differentiation
Centered spatial difference
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
Use analytic Jv, a two-residual central difference, or one-direction forward AD. Apply a Poisson Thomas right preconditioner with two-pass reorthogonalized GMRES/Givens. Start eta=.3, then clamp .9*(Fk/Fk-1)^1.5 to [.001,.5]. This is an explicit EW Choice2-style variant, not the paper’s full safeguards or PETSc defaults.
Bratu nonlinear boundary-value problem
The same dimensionless one-dimensional Dirichlet problem at lambda=3, 63/127 interior nodes, starting from zero or 4sin(pi*x). Twelve mode/grid/branch solves plus one analytic-Jv constant-eta=1e-8 control. GMRES restart24/max96, at most 24 Newton steps and nonlinear tolerance1e-9.
Problem figure
A saved validation figure for this execution example. Its conditions and acceptance scope are documented by this page’s checks.

This problem’s code and validation status
Exact / reference solutions
References and checks for this execution
Reference and validation scope

Same-problem reference · Analytic reference
Jacobian-free Newton–Krylov with analytic, central-FD and directional-AD products
An educational small1D BVP. AD covers only elementary arithmetic, exp and linear boundary padding. Small Hessenberg matrices and Krylov bases are stored. ## Bratu fold continuation and Jacobian-free Newton-Krylov — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-bratu-continuation-jfnk/#bratu-matrix-free-jfnk-assumptions

The same dimensionless one-dimensional Dirichlet problem at lambda=3, 63/127 interior nodes, starting from zero or 4sin(pi*x). Twelve mode/grid/branch solves plus one analytic-Jv constant-eta=1e-8 control. GMRES restart24/max96, at most 24 Newton steps and nonlinear tolerance1e-9.

## Bratu fold continuation and Jacobian-free Newton-Krylov — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-bratu-continuation-jfnk/#bratu-matrix-free-jfnk-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Use analytic Jv, a two-residual central difference, or one-direction forward AD. Apply a Poisson Thomas right preconditioner with two-pass reorthogonalized GMRES/Givens. Start eta=.3, then clamp .9*(Fk/Fk-1)^1.5 to [.001,.5]. This is an explicit EW Choice2-style variant, not the paper’s full safeguards or PETSc defaults.
-u''=\lambda e^u,\quad u(0)=u(1)=0u_\theta=2\log\frac{\cosh(\theta/2)}{\cosh(\theta(x-1/2))},\quad\lambda(\theta)=2\theta^2/\cosh^2(\theta/2)J(u)v=A_hv-\lambda e^u\odot v\eta_k=\min\{0.5,\max\{0.001,0.9(\|F_k\|_2/\|F_{k-1}\|_2)^{1.5}\}\}

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-coefficient-diffusion/#rotated-anisotropic-diffusion-algorithm

Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
HLL
Heun / SSPRK(2,2)
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
The published Numart piecewise-constant HLL flux, unsplit x/y divergence and Heun/SSPRK(2,2) form a small standalone package with both-stage boundary accounting and state checks. CFL.4 uses the sum of directional maximum acoustic rates; the top boundary uses each actual RK stage time. No state floor, repair or hidden retry. Invalid stages retain raw arrays/history and fail.
Compressible Euler equations
Two-dimensional compressible Euler conservation laws with gamma1.4. This example fixes the Mach10 incident shock, inflow/outflow, reflecting wall and moving-shock top boundary.
Problem figure
A saved validation figure for this execution example. Its conditions and acceptance scope are documented by this page’s checks.

## Double Mach reflection: lightweight grid verification — Double Mach reflection: lightweight grid verification [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-double-mach/
Coverage: reading

References and checks for this execution
Reference and validation scope
The original preregistered20 unit tests passed. Before the full three-grid run, read-only review added an absent-front diagnostic guard and one test; the old contract/source are preserved and a revision contract was frozen. All21 tests, three final-time runs and40 gates passed with-W error. Previously independently executed Ny64/128 primitive MUSCL/generalized-minmod theta1.5/HLL/Heun data from the RKDG kit are reused; no reference PDE was rerun. Density L1 differences from conservatively restricted Ny128 are.08431/.05802/.03503 and pressure differences.09556/.06798/.04156. Reference64/128 increments are.00955/.01250, about.273/.301 of the finest primary differences. Maximum relative four-component boundary-budget residual is about4.60e-13.
Same-problem reference · Finite-grid numerical reference
Double Mach reflection: saved independent finite-grid numerical reference
Compare against two previously independently executed finite-volume reference grids using conservative restriction. This is a finite-grid numerical reference, not an exact2D solution or error bound.

## Double Mach reflection: lightweight grid verification — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-double-mach/#double-mach-reflection-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Nondimensional[0,4]x[0,1], gamma1.4, Mach10. Shock footx=1/6, angle60degrees; postshock(rho,u,v,p)=(8,8.25sqrt(3)/2,-4.125,116.5), upstream(1.4,0,0,1). Initial cells are classified by their centers, not exact cut-cell means. Left postshock inflow, right zero-gradient, bottom postshock forx<1/6 and slip wall otherwise; top postshock forx<1/6+(1+20t)/sqrt(3).

## Double Mach reflection: lightweight grid verification — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-double-mach/#double-mach-reflection-algorithm
Coverage: reading

The published Numart piecewise-constant HLL flux, unsplit x/y divergence and Heun/SSPRK(2,2) form a small standalone package with both-stage boundary accounting and state checks. CFL.4 uses the sum of directional maximum acoustic rates; the top boundary uses each actual RK stage time. No state floor, repair or hidden retry. Invalid stages retain raw arrays/history and fail.
\partial_tU+\partial_xF(U)+\partial_yG(U)=0,\qquad U=(\rho,\rho u,\rho v,E)^Tx_s(y,t)=\frac16+\frac{y+20t}{\sqrt3},\quad \gamma=1.4,\quad M_s=10\Delta t=0.4\left[\max(|u|+c)/\Delta x+\max(|v|+c)/\Delta y\right]^{-1}\sum_{ij}|C_{ij}|(\bar U_{ij}^{n+1}-\bar U_{ij}^{n})=\frac{\Delta t}{2}(B(U^n,t_n)+B(U^{(1)},t_n+\Delta t))

## Double Mach reflection: lightweight grid verification — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-double-mach/#double-mach-reflection-validation
Coverage: reading

The original preregistered20 unit tests passed. Before the full three-grid run, read-only review added an absent-front diagnostic guard and one test; the old contract/source are preserved and a revision contract was frozen. All21 tests, three final-time runs and40 gates passed with-W error. Previously independently executed Ny64/128 primitive MUSCL/generalized-minmod theta1.5/HLL/Heun data from the RKDG kit are reused; no reference PDE was rerun. Density L1 differences from conservatively restricted Ny128 are.08431/.05802/.03503 and pressure differences.09556/.06798/.04156. Reference64/128 increments are.00955/.01250, about.273/.301 of the finest primary differences. Maximum relative four-component boundary-budget residual is about4.60e-13.

## Double Mach reflection: lightweight grid verification — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-double-mach/#double-mach-reflection-limits
Coverage: reading

The reference is finite-grid numerical data, not an exact2D solution or an Athena/LAVA execution. The HLL family is shared, but reference spatial operators are separately written and not imported by the primary. The reference increment is an uncertainty diagnostic, not an error bound. Initial projection, sampled moving boundaries, discretization and finite-reference effects all enter the difference; the slope is no rigorous order or full reflection-pattern convergence proof. The upper-front discrepancy stays2cells while its physical width shrinks. Fixed near-wall ROIx in[1,2.75],y<=.25 is not feature tracking. Finest ROI maxu12.644 versus reference16.125 shows the thin wall jet/roll-up is unresolved. Forward step, other wall data, general perturbations, higher order and full-pattern convergence are unverified.

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-dsmc-shock/
Coverage: reading

Disjoint cell-local random pairs with even/odd finite-N physical-time sigma*g acceptance,energy-based safe majorant and predeclared bounded subcycling; no probability caps. Exact flight-to-wall and flux-conditioned diffuse/reservoir velocities with remaining flight time. Open-reservoir macro counts use unbiased floor(mean)+Bernoulli(fraction) per face/species/half-stream to reduce artificial sampling variance; no Poisson number-fluctuation or thermodynamic-fluctuation reproduction claim. Retain the original four seeds and append the next eight consecutive seeds; uniform permutation/stable integer sorting preserves the ideal within-cell matching law,not RNG consumption or bit-identical trajectories. Edition2026-11-24 only reuses immutable reservoir coefficients and an inverse-CDF residual at unchanged v,fuses concatenation in unchanged keep-left-right order,and reversibly narrows range-checked integer sort keys to uint8 before the same stable sort. Original permutation/RNG calls,equal-key particle order,collision pairs and scientific inputs remain unchanged. The first three changes passed163component checks; a separate348check study qualifies the sort-key composition with exact byte/RNG comparisons. Neither is a new main run; full saved-science equality remains pending.

## Finite-Knudsen Couette and Fourier flows — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-dsmc-wall/#dsmc-couette-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Disjoint cell-local random pairs with even/odd finite-N physical-time sigma*g acceptance,energy-based safe majorant and predeclared bounded subcycling; no probability caps. Exact flight-to-wall and flux-conditioned diffuse/reservoir velocities with remaining flight time.
\partial_t f+v_x\partial_x f=Q_{\mathrm{HS}}(f,f),\quad \sigma=\pi d^2=1/\sqrt{2}P_{ij}=n\langle c_i c_j\rangle,\quad q_x=\frac{n}{2}\langle c_x|\mathbf c|^2\rangle,\quad\mathbf c=\mathbf v-\mathbf up_{ij}=a_N W\sigma g_{ij}\Delta t/V,\quad a_N=\begin{cases}N-1&N\text{ even}\\N&N\text{ odd}\end{cases}g_{ij}\le\sqrt{2\sum_i|\mathbf v_i-\mathbf v_{cm}|^2}

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-euler-positivity/
Coverage: reading

Evolve the existing strong double rarefaction on 128/256/512 cells, connecting mean-preserving positivity scaling to MUSCL, global LF fluxes and SSPRK(3,3). Log density, pressure and boundary budgets for every FE substep and SSP convex combination.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Lax–Friedrichs
MUSCL reconstruction
Mean-preserving positive-state scaling
SSPRK(3,3)
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
Unlimited conservative central linear reconstruction is scaled toward its mean with one common theta per cell until both endpoint densities/pressures are positive. The two endpoint mean remains the original conserved mean. Shared LF FE updates are combined by SSPRK(3,3), reconstructing/limiting before every flux stage. Epsilon1e-13 is a reconstruction target, not an injected density/energy floor. No average repair or hidden time-step retries are used.
Compressible Euler equations
Unforced one-dimensional ideal-gas Euler at gamma=1.4 evolves cell means of density, momentum and total energy using linear conservative MUSCL reconstruction and shared Lax–Friedrichs fluxes.

## Euler double rarefaction: positivity at every stage — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-euler-positivity/#euler-double-rarefaction-positivity-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Fix gamma1.4, x in [0,1], discontinuity x0=.5, outer primitive states(1,-2,.4)/(1,2,.4) and T=.15. The low-density central state remains strictly positive; this is not a vacuum-generating case. Use fixed global LF splitting speed a4 and dt*a/dx<=.4; assert every actual endpoint satisfies |u|+c<=a and the sufficient dt*a/dx<=1/2 condition.

## Euler double rarefaction: positivity at every stage — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-euler-positivity/#euler-double-rarefaction-positivity-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Unlimited conservative central linear reconstruction is scaled toward its mean with one common theta per cell until both endpoint densities/pressures are positive. The two endpoint mean remains the original conserved mean. Shared LF FE updates are combined by SSPRK(3,3), reconstructing/limiting before every flux stage. Epsilon1e-13 is a reconstruction target, not an injected density/energy floor. No average repair or hidden time-step retries are used.
\partial_t U+\partial_x F(U)=0,\qquad U=(\rho,m,E)^T,\quad F=(m,m^2/\rho+p,(E+p)m/\rho)^T,\quad p=(\gamma-1)(E-m^2/(2\rho))U_i^{\pm}=\bar U_i\pm\delta U_i,\qquad\widehat U_i^{\pm}=\bar U_i+\theta_i(U_i^{\pm}-\bar U_i),\quad0\le\theta_i\le1,\qquad\tfrac12(\widehat U_i^-+\widehat U_i^+)=\bar U_i\widehat F_{i+1/2}=\tfrac12\!\left[F(\widehat U_i^+)+F(\widehat U_{i+1}^-)-a(\widehat U_{i+1}^--\widehat U_i^+)\right],\qquad\mathcal E_{\Delta t}(\bar U)_i=\bar U_i-\frac{\Delta t}{\Delta x}(\widehat F_{i+1/2}-\widehat F_{i-1/2})U^{(1)}=\mathcal E_{\Delta t}(U^n),\qquad U^{(2)}=\tfrac34U^n+\tfrac14\mathcal E_{\Delta t}(U^{(1)}),\qquad U^{n+1}=\tfrac13U^n+\tfrac23\mathcal E_{\Delta t}(U^{(2)})a\ge\max_{i,\pm}(|u(\widehat U_i^\pm)|+c(\widehat U_i^\pm)),\qquad\frac{a\Delta t}{\Delta x}\le\tfrac12,\qquad\rho(\widehat U_i^\pm)>0,\quad p(\widehat U_i^\pm)>0

## Euler double rarefaction: positivity at every stage — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-euler-positivity/#euler-double-rarefaction-positivity-limits
Coverage: reading

Evidence covers this one P1 FV update and fixed input, not general MUSCL/WENO/DG, characteristic reconstruction, reflecting walls, vacuum generation or multidimensional positivity. Unlimited central slopes have no TVD, maximum-principle or nonoscillation guarantee. Raw pressure is evaluated only where raw density is positive; nonpositive raw density has its own count. Reference pressure is p(mean conserved q), not mean pressure. Gallery plots are saved one-dimensional x-t fields, not two-dimensional flow. No ExactPack or separate PDE engine is executed.

Xiangxiong Zhang and Chi-Wang Shu (2010). On positivity-preserving high order discontinuous Galerkin schemes for compressible Euler equations on rectangular meshes [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.1016/j.jcp.2010.08.016
Review scope / review_level: author manuscript selected sections actually inspected: §2 Theorem2.1, Remarks2.2/2.4/2.6/2.7; §4.3 distinguishes vacuum input

David I. Ketcheson, Randall J. LeVeque and Mauricio J. del Razo (2020). Riemann Problems and Jupyter Solutions: The Euler equations of gas dynamics [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.1137/1.9781611976212

## Mach-3 forward-facing step: lightweight 2D verification — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-forward-step/#forward-step-m3-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Published Numart piecewise-constant HLL, unsplit x/y divergence and Heun/SSPRK(2,2) become a standalone package. Six boundary categories integrate the actual fluxes at both RK stages with identical weights. CFL.4, at most20000steps per grid. Every predictor/update checks positive density and pressure. No state floor, repair or hidden retry; invalid stages retain raw arrays/completed history and fail.
\partial_tU+\partial_xF(U)+\partial_yG(U)=0,\qquad U=(\rho,\rho u,\rho v,E)^T\Omega=([0,3]\times[0,1])\setminus([0.6,3]\times[0,0.2]),\quad (\rho,u,v,p)_\infty=(1.4,3,0,1)\sum_{C\subset\Omega}|C|(\bar U_C^{n+1}-\bar U_C^n)=\frac{\Delta t}{2}(B(U^n)+B(U^{(1)})),\quad B=-\sum_{\partial\Omega}|f|\widehat F_n\epsilon_1(\rho)=\frac{\sum_{C\subset\Omega}|\bar\rho_C-\overline{\rho_{\rm ref}}_C|}{\sum_{C\subset\Omega}|\overline{\rho_{\rm ref}}_C|}

## Mach-3 forward-facing step: lightweight 2D verification — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-forward-step/#forward-step-m3-limits
Coverage: reading

The reference is separately implemented but shares the HLL family and Heun; no external AMROC,LAVA or RKDG engine was executed. Finite-grid numerical data are neither an exact2D solution nor an error bound. Without special corner treatment, a numerical entropy layer may be advected downstream; no agreement with corrected originalPPM fine structures is claimed. Whole-fluid differences,Linf and fixed corner density/pressure/entropy diagnostics are retained. Slopes do not prove pure spatial order; thin slip lines,roll-up,general geometries and high-order convergence remain unverified. Normalized maximum density differences=.592/.670/.665 do not decrease. Corner minima of log(p/rho^gamma)=-.0784/-.1224/-.3510 change substantially. This absolute entropy variable includes an arbitrary additive constant; a more-negative value is not itself an error increase. Neither stable corner extrema nor pointwise pattern convergence is established.

## Numerical foundations: conditioning, residuals, convergence and independent references — AMG: conditioning, anisotropy, residual and forward error [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations-conditioning/
Coverage: reading

Store true residual, forward error, DST agreement, operator complexity and complete histories. Perturb a maximal-eigenmode RHS in the minimal-eigenmode direction and check the predicted relative amplification κ₂ with direct solves. Isotropic runs must converge; the predeclared anisotropy stress policy permits honestly reported budget exhaustion. A one-cycle control detects nonconvergence.
No corresponding reference-library card is registered. The execution-specific validation material above documents its reference values and acceptance checks.

## Numerical foundations: conditioning, residuals, convergence and independent references — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations-conditioning/#amg-conditioning-assumptions
Coverage: reading

A=T⊗I+εI⊗T with n=7/15/31 and ε=1/.1/.01. This is a known-solution algebraic diagnostic; continuum PDE validation remains in the earlier Poisson example. At fixed square n, κ₂ is independent of ε.

## Numerical foundations: conditioning, residuals, convergence and independent references — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations-conditioning/#amg-conditioning-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Reuse the earlier MIT-licensed Atlas educational smoothed-aggregation AMG in a separate source release. Matrix-only hierarchy setup uses strength .08, Jacobi smoothing, fixed relative tolerance 10⁻¹⁰ and at most 180 V-cycles. Sine-transform spectral inversion is reference-side only.
\kappa_2(A)=\cot^2\!\left(\frac{\pi}{2(n+1)}\right)\frac{\|x-\hat x\|_2}{\|x\|_2}\le\kappa_2(A)\frac{\|b-A\hat x\|_2}{\|b\|_2}

## Numerical foundations: conditioning, residuals, convergence and independent references — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations-conditioning/#amg-conditioning-limits
Coverage: reading

Only a small constant-coefficient family is checked. Arbitrary coefficient jumps, unstructured grids, indefinite systems, optimal complexity and uniform convergence are outside scope. No claim that anisotropy necessarily increases κ₂ or monotonically worsens convergence.

## Numerical foundations: conditioning, residuals, convergence and independent references — QR/SVD: prescribed spectra, perturbation gain and numerical rank [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations-conditioning/
Coverage: reading

Save reconstruction, orthogonality, singular values, solution perturbations, least-squares stationarity and an exact rank-two control. The mpmath1.3.0 SVD and QR reference was actually executed using integer-ratio conversions of binary inputs. Runtime SHA and completeness guards check all four inputs at both precisions and never substitute analytic truth after a mismatch.
No corresponding reference-library card is registered. The execution-specific validation material above documents its reference values and acceptance checks.

## Numerical foundations: conditioning, residuals, convergence and independent references — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations-conditioning/#qr-svd-conditioning-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Use Hadamard orthogonal factors U,V and sⱼ=2⁻qj for q=0/4/8/12. Fixed b=u₀ and b+2⁻⁴⁰u_min measure perturbation amplification. Individual singular vectors are nonunique for the repeated singular values at q=0.

## Numerical foundations: conditioning, residuals, convergence and independent references — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations-conditioning/#qr-svd-conditioning-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Implement Householder QR, one-sided Jacobi SVD and triangular back substitution. Vary rank cutoffs 10⁻⁸/10⁻¹²/10⁻¹⁴ and compare with LAPACK solutions using the same truncation convention. No executed normal-equations comparison is added.
A=U\operatorname{diag}(2^{-qj})V^T,\quad\kappa_2(A)=2^{3q}\delta b=\eta u_{\min},\quad\delta x=\eta\sigma_{\min}^{-1}v_{\min}

Some LAPACK and projected-core numerical infrastructure is shared. mpmath SVD uses separate bidiagonalization and QR iteration; mpmath least squares is a separate high-precision implementation of the same Householder family. Tiny-singular-value relative accuracy is not guaranteed for arbitrary ill-conditioned matrices.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Matrix-based AMG: distinguish residual and solution error [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/
Coverage: reading

Build a smoothed-aggregation hierarchy from an SPD matrix alone and run V-cycles. Problems with 7², 15² and 31² unknowns distinguish independent sparse direct solutions, analytic discrete sine modes and second-order convergence to the continuum solution.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Algebraic multigrid / AMG
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
A graph based on row-relative off-diagonal strength supplies greedy star aggregates; leftover nodes attach to adjacent aggregates. Smooth tentative T via P=(I−ωD⁻¹A)T with ω=4/(3ρ̄), where ρ̄ bounds the absolute row sums of D⁻¹A. Coarse operators are PᵀAP. V-cycles use two pre/post Jacobi sweeps and a terminal dense direct solve. This is a small adopted SA variant, not every construction or convergence theorem in the original paper.
No corresponding equation-registry entry is registered. The example-specific definition above supplies its formulation, approximation or diagnostic.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Matrix-based AMG: distinguish residual and solution error [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/
Coverage: reading

References and checks for this execution
Reference and validation scope
Store normalized residuals, relative solution differences against SciPy spsolve, discrete-L²-type continuum errors, observed order and operator complexity. A randomly permuted matrix is also checked against a direct solution to expose hidden geometric ordering assumptions. A zero cycle budget reports nonconvergence.
Related-model reference · Manufactured solution
Poisson / manufactured sine
The card is 1D sin(πx); this test is 2D sin(πx)sin(πy). Dimension, forcing and FEM error norms differ.
Same-problem reference · Manufactured solution
2D Poisson sine manufactured solution: shared SEM/P1 FEM reference
Dimensionless: -Laplacian u=2pi²sin(pi x)sin(pi y) on[0,1]², u=0 on the boundary. Constant coefficient; affine Cartesian squares for SEM and the existing regular triangle mesh for P1 FEM.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#sa-amg-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Dimensionless unit square, constant-positive-coefficient −Δu=f, homogeneous Dirichlet boundaries and five-point differences. Hierarchy setup receives no coordinates, mesh width or n; it uses the coefficient matrix and an implicit constant near-null candidate. A real SPD input is assumed; arbitrary indefinite problems are outside scope.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#sa-amg-algorithm
Coverage: reading

A graph based on row-relative off-diagonal strength supplies greedy star aggregates; leftover nodes attach to adjacent aggregates. Smooth tentative T via P=(I−ωD⁻¹A)T with ω=4/(3ρ̄), where ρ̄ bounds the absolute row sums of D⁻¹A. Coarse operators are PᵀAP. V-cycles use two pre/post Jacobi sweeps and a terminal dense direct solve. This is a small adopted SA variant, not every construction or convergence theorem in the original paper.
A_c=P^TAP,\quad P=(I-\omega D^{-1}A)Tr_k=b-Ax_k,\quad \eta_k=\|r_k\|_2/\|b\|_2

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#sa-amg-limits

Only three fixed scalar grids are checked. Large coefficient jumps, strong anisotropy, elasticity, arbitrary unstructured meshes, optimal complexity and mesh-independent convergence are not certified. A small residual alone does not prove a small solution error.

This example’s formulation and conditions

Householder reflectors triangularize R while accumulating Q. ## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#qr-svd-factorization-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Small real matrices with m≥n. Numerical rank uses a 10⁻¹² threshold relative to the largest singular value; compact factors omit null directions. QR has no column pivoting and is not used as a rank-revealing method.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#qr-svd-factorization-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Householder reflectors triangularize R while accumulating Q. The SVD repeatedly rotates column pairs toward orthogonality and uses their resulting lengths as singular values; it does not diagonalize AᵀA. Least squares uses triangular back substitution for QR and truncated compact SVD for deficient rank.
A=QR,\quad Q^TQ=IA\simeq U_r\Sigma_rV_r^T,\quad x_{\min}=V_r\Sigma_r^{-1}U_r^Tb

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#krylov-eigenvalues-assumptions

The symmetric case is real symmetric; the nonsymmetric case is real with a known separated largest eigenvalue 5. Starting vectors use fixed seeds. Nonsymmetric Ritz values may be complex and are selected by largest real part.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#krylov-eigenvalues-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Lanczos uses its three-term recurrence plus two passes of full reorthogonalization; Arnoldi uses two-pass modified Gram–Schmidt. Only the small projected T/H is solved by NumPy eigh/eig before lifting Ritz vectors. A full dense solve of the original matrix is used only on the reference side.
AV_m=V_mH_m+h_{m+1,m}v_{m+1}e_m^TH_my=\theta y,\quad v=V_my,\quad r=Av-\theta v

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Gauss–Legendre and adaptive quadrature: exactness, error estimates and budgets [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/

Measure polynomial moments for every chosen order, node/weight differences from SciPy roots_legendre, order refinement for the analytic exponential integral, and agreement with analytic arctangent and SciPy quad references. ## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#gauss-adaptive-quadrature-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Dimensionless smooth real functions on finite intervals. Fixed Gauss orders 2/4/8/16 and adaptive absolute tolerances 10⁻⁵/10⁻⁷/10⁻⁹ are swept separately. Endpoint singularities, discontinuities and infinite intervals are not covered by these inputs.

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#gauss-adaptive-quadrature-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Golub–Welsch obtains nodes from a symmetric Jacobi matrix and weights from twice the squared first eigenvector components. Adaptive Simpson bisects intervals and allocates tolerances using |Sleft+Sright−Swhole|/15 as a local estimate. Evaluation and depth limits report unmet targets explicitly.
\int_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,dx\simeq\sum_{j=1}^{n}w_jf(x_j)E_{\mathrm{est}}=|S_{\mathrm{left}}+S_{\mathrm{right}}-S_{\mathrm{whole}}|/15

## AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-foundations/#gauss-adaptive-quadrature-limits
Coverage: reading

The local Simpson estimate is not a rigorous error bound for arbitrary functions. The implementation does not generally solve missed high frequencies, singularities or roundoff stagnation, and it is not a reimplementation of Gauss–Kronrod or all of QUADPACK.

## Geometric integration of constraints, orbits and multiple frequencies — SHAKE and RATTLE: constraints and momentum ownership [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-geometric-controls/
Coverage: reading

Ten fixed pendulum evolutions distinguish position constraints, full-time tangent momentum and interior centered momentum.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
SHAKE constrained integration
RATTLE constrained integration
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
Original scalar Newton position constraints, RATTLE final tangent impulses and SHAKE position pairs. SHAKE momentum is centered only at interior nodes; endpoint momenta are absent. SHAKE solves columns are eta, eta/h^2, position residual and Newton updates. Column1 uses the uniform recurrence normalization eta/h^2. For the first constrained half-step startup, the physical multiplier is 2*eta/h^2; later full position-Verlet steps use eta/h^2. Reverse-pair steps all use the later recurrence convention. RATTLE has its separate five-column normalization. No scientific gate or plot uses SHAKE column1.
Constrained planar pendulum
L=m=g=1, initial angle 0.7 and zero angular velocity. C=(q·q−1)/2, T=100 and h=0.04/0.02/0.01; position targets are fixed at 1e−13, with a coarse 1e−10 companion.

Coverage: reading

An independent Kepler-equation family, qualified with brentq and bisection, supports 92 main decisions: full-state error, energy/angular momentum, at least eight periapses, finite-window order and reversal defects.

## Geometric integration of constraints, orbits and multiple frequencies — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-geometric-controls/#kepler-eccentricity-limits
Coverage: reading

Small invariant errors do not establish phase accuracy. No canonical symplectic-defect measurement is claimed for the variable-step map, and fixed-h properties are not transferred automatically. R1 resolution was revised to R2 using pre-execution asymptotic planning, not measured calibration.

## Geometric integration of constraints, orbits and multiple frequencies — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-geometric-controls/#kepler-eccentricity-references
Coverage: reading

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
Lecture2: Symplectic integrators [accessed 2026-11-24]
Review scope / review_level: selected-primary-scope
Author-hosted course notes, selected rendered printed pages2,12–13: Verlet kick/drift form, symplectic statement, Lie and symmetric Strang compositions. This does not qualify every state-dependent step rule or the authored coupled resonance experiment.
Approximate Positions of the Planets [accessed 2026-11-24]
Review scope / review_level: selected-primary-scope
Official JPL page, selected steps3–4 and Kepler equation. Only the eccentric-anomaly equation and elliptic coordinate transformation are used; no planetary coefficient tables, fitted ephemeris accuracy or Horizons calculation is claimed. Publication date was not verified.

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-geometric-controls/
Coverage: reading

A genuinely coupled two-degree-of-freedom system uses twelve 64-step probes and six accuracy trajectories to separate normal modes, coordinate exchange, discrete maps and roundoff.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used

Strang splitting
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Full-potential Verlet and a Strang impulse composition: half B kick, exact A flow, half B kick. A contains the fast oscillator and slow free drift; B contains the slow potential and the coupling.
Coupled two-frequency harmonic oscillators
alpha=1, omega=10/20, q0=(1,1/omega) and p0=0. Central probes retain the evaluated binary64 h and sin/cos coefficients without snapping to mathematical pi.

## Geometric integration of constraints, orbits and multiple frequencies — Coupled frequencies and finite-window resonance [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-geometric-controls/
Coverage: reading

The 116 main decisions distinguish independent coupled normal modes, Decimal80/120 and Fraction frozen-coefficient maps, and stagewise gamma8 roundoff allowances. Ideal-pi Jordan structure is checked separately by rational identities. Each probe uses the current saved coefficient hex for its own Decimal80/120 actions; six accuracy actions use Decimal80.
Same-problem reference · Semi-analytic reference
Coupled frequencies and finite-window resonance
The central actual floating map remains unresolved; ideal-pi Jordan structure is not transferred to it. Results concern 64-step amplification and small fixed inputs, not a scanned resonance diagram, general stability or a universal long-time error theorem.

## Geometric integration of constraints, orbits and multiple frequencies — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-geometric-controls/#multifrequency-resonance-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Full-potential Verlet and a Strang impulse composition: half B kick, exact A flow, half B kick. A contains the fast oscillator and slow free drift; B contains the slow potential and the coupling.
H=\tfrac12(p_1^2+p_2^2+q_1^2+\omega^2q_2^2)+\alpha q_1q_2\Phi_h=\varphi^B_{h/2}\circ\varphi^A_h\circ\varphi^B_{h/2}\chi_{\theta=\pi}(z)=(z+1)^2[z^2-(2-h^2)z+1]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-guderley/
Coverage: reading

HLL plus Heun follows a Guderley shock into stationary zero-pressure upstream gas at gamma=1.4, r in [0,0.75], t=-1 to -0.85 on 128/256/512 shells. Initialize the similarity field with Rs(-1)=0.6 and compare the pre-collapse trajectory, conserved shell means and budgets with a semi-analytic reference. The figure is a 2D section display of 1D radial results.

## Guderley converging shock: lightweight spherical-radial verification — Guderley converging shock: lightweight spherical-radial verification [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-guderley/
Coverage: reading

An inward spherical Guderley shock in cold stationary gas is evolved from t=-1 to -0.85 on 128/256/512 radial shells. HLL fluxes and Heun steps are checked against a similarity eigenvalue/field, shock trajectory and discrete conservation budgets.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
HLL
Heun / SSPRK(2,2)
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
First-order spherical finite volumes use face area4pi*r^2 and shell volume4pi*delta(r^3)/3. Shared HLL flux divergence plus the radial-momentum pressure source p_i*delta(A)/V is advanced by Heun at CFL0.4. The center is reflecting with zero face area; the outer similarity state is evaluated at both actual RK times. All three conserved budgets integrate the actual boundary flux and geometric source using the same Heun weights. There are no state floors, pressure repairs or hidden step retries.
Compressible Euler equations
The one-dimensional spherical-radial ideal-gas Euler system with zero upstream pressure and gamma=1.4. The fixed input defines a pre-collapse interval, similarity initial field, boundaries and shell averaging.

## Guderley converging shock: lightweight spherical-radial verification — Guderley converging shock: lightweight spherical-radial verification [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-guderley/
Coverage: reading

The pre-collapse branch of the spherical Guderley similarity solution at gamma=1.4 with a cold uniform upstream state. Eigenvalue shooting, similarity-ODE integration and shock-split shell quadrature make it semi-analytic rather than closed-form exact cell means. Routine replay reuses lambda from the retained qualification, freshly integrating the similarity ODE and quadrature; recomputing the eigenvalue and original ExactPack probes is a separate explicit command. This is an adapter to pinned ExactPack, not an independently implemented similarity evaluator. Collapse at the origin, the reflected shock and general equations of state remain outside this example.

## Guderley converging shock: lightweight spherical-radial verification — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-guderley/#guderley-implosion-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Fix gamma=1.4, three-dimensional spherical symmetry on r in [0,0.75], Rs(-1)=0.6 and t in [-1,-0.85]. Ahead of the inward shock the inner gas is exactly rho0=1,u0=p0=0. The outer region already contains the shocked similarity field; the entire initial domain is not a uniform cold state. Initial conserved shell means use order16 Gauss integration split at the exact shock, checked against order32. Reference pressure is p(mean conserved state), not mean primitive pressure.

## Guderley converging shock: lightweight spherical-radial verification — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-guderley/#guderley-implosion-algorithm
Coverage: reading

First-order spherical finite volumes use face area4pi*r^2 and shell volume4pi*delta(r^3)/3. Shared HLL flux divergence plus the radial-momentum pressure source p_i*delta(A)/V is advanced by Heun at CFL0.4. The center is reflecting with zero face area; the outer similarity state is evaluated at both actual RK times. All three conserved budgets integrate the actual boundary flux and geometric source using the same Heun weights. There are no state floors, pressure repairs or hidden step retries.
\partial_t U+\frac{1}{r^2}\partial_r(r^2 F)=\left(0,\frac{2p}{r},0\right)^T,\quad U=(\rho,\rho u,E)^TR_s(t)=0.6(-t)^\alpha,\quad\alpha=1/\lambda,\quad \lambda\simeq1.3943607844,\quad t<0\frac{d\bar U_i}{dt}=-\frac{A_{i+1/2}\widehat F_{i+1/2}-A_{i-1/2}\widehat F_{i-1/2}}{V_i}+\left(0,p_i\frac{\Delta A_i}{V_i},0\right)^T\bar U_i^{\rm ref}=\frac{\int_{r_{i-1/2}}^{r_{i+1/2}}U_{\rm sim}(r,t)r^2\,dr}{(r_{i+1/2}^3-r_{i-1/2}^3)/3},\qquad p_i^{\rm ref}=p(\bar U_i^{\rm ref})

## Guderley converging shock: lightweight spherical-radial verification — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-guderley/#guderley-implosion-limits
Coverage: reading

This is a short one-dimensional spherical verification away from collapse t=0. The singular origin, reflected branch, cylindrical geometry, other gammas and nonspherical perturbation stability are untested. Two-dimensional pictures map saved spherical shell means onto a meridional plane; they are not Cartesian2D evolution. The semi-analytic field is a numerically evaluated ODE/quadrature reference, not a closed-form exact cell average. Zero pressure is allowed in the cold upstream; cancellation-band negative internal energy density down to an absolute64eps is recorded. Sound-speed square-root guards only within that band have separate counts/minimum raw pressure and do not repair the state. No general nonlinear positivity theorem is claimed. Shock-position error in cell units does not decrease monotonically:1.13/2.27/2.54. Absolute radius error is about0.00665 for the first two grids and0.00372 for the finest. Density Linf differences0.258/0.271/0.266 and pressure Linf0.492/0.494/0.466 are also not monotonically decreasing. L1 reduction is not evidence that the discontinuity is pointwise resolved or that the collapse region converges.

The LANL record and abstract distinguish the convergence exponent from the reflected trajectory eigenvalue. This is not a claim to have read the entire paper or reproduced its PDE experiment; the present field is constructed using the pinned ExactPack source.
Roger B. Lazarus (1981). Self-Similar Solutions for Converging Shocks and Collapsing Cavities [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.1137/0718022
Review scope / review_level: publisher bibliographic record/abstract plus equations2.5,2.8,2.9 and sphericalTable6.5 as explicitly transcribed in pinned ExactPack; original full text not inspected
Checked the publisher record/abstract and the explicitly attributed equations/table in ExactPack. The tabulated lambda1.3943607838 is the value transcribed in that code, not an independent retranscription of the original table.
R. F. Chisnell (1998). An analytic description of converging shock waves [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.1017/S0022112097007775
Review scope / review_level: publisher bibliographic record/abstract and equation3.1 implementation/comments in actual pinned ExactPack eexp source
Checked the publisher record/abstract and the critical-point phase matching and equation3.1 implementation in ExactPack eexp. The exponent is computed through that eigenvalue routine rather than fixed by dimensional analysis.

## KH/RT initial growth and independent linear references — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-instability-growth/#kh-initial-growth-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Advance point-sampled perturbations using centered shared-face conservative fluxes and Heun; invert the five-point Poisson symbol by FFT. Centered derivatives define divergence-free velocity. Analytic base subtraction avoids a discretization imbalance larger than the small perturbation.
-\Delta\psi=\omega,\qquad (u,v)=(\partial_y\psi,-\partial_x\psi)U(y)=\tanh(\sin y/\delta),\quad \omega_t+U\omega_x+U^{\prime\prime}\psi_x+\mathbf{u}\cdot\nabla\omega=\nu\Delta\omega\sigma_T=\frac{1}{T}\log\frac{A(T)}{A(0)},\qquad \dot{\widehat{\mathbf{q}}}=L_K\widehat{\mathbf{q}}

Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Gradient and quasi-Newton optimization
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Original inverse-BFGS and vector-only two-loop L-BFGS with three pairs. A separate small dense oracle replays only currently retained pairs from the current gamma0 I. SciPy BFGS and unbounded L-BFGS-B are distinct software companions.
Finite-dimensional algebraic optimization and known minima
Dimensionless unconstrained algebraic optimization with known analytic minima; there is no physical PDE boundary condition.

A saved validation figure for this execution example. Its conditions and acceptance scope are documented by this page’s checks.
BFGS and three-pair L-BFGS at known minima

Exact / reference solutions
References and checks for this execution
Sixteen fixed fits check analytic minima/gradients, strong Wolfe and resolved positive curvature at every accepted step, symmetric SPD BFGS matrices and L-BFGS action defects. Retained-pair and dense-oracle storage are reported separately.

Coverage: reading

Original inverse-BFGS and vector-only two-loop L-BFGS with three pairs. A separate small dense oracle replays only currently retained pairs from the current gamma0 I. SciPy BFGS and unbounded L-BFGS-B are distinct software companions.
H_+=(I-\rho s y^T)H(I-\rho y s^T)+\rho s s^T\rho=(y^Ts)^{-1},\quad\gamma_0=(s^Ty)/(y^Ty)f(x,y)=100(y-x^2)^2+(1-x)^2

## Optimization, noise and regularization in the Bratu inverse problem — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-inverse-optimization/#bfgs-lbfgs-controls-validation
Coverage: reading

Sixteen fixed fits check analytic minima/gradients, strong Wolfe and resolved positive curvature at every accepted step, symmetric SPD BFGS matrices and L-BFGS action defects. Retained-pair and dense-oracle storage are reported separately.

## Optimization, noise and regularization in the Bratu inverse problem — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-inverse-optimization/#bfgs-lbfgs-controls-limits
Coverage: reading

No exact n-step termination or general global convergence on Rosenbrock is claimed. The selected original text uses weak Wolfe, distinct from this study’s strong Wolfe policy. Fletcher’s 1970 original article remains unread.

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
On the limited memory BFGS method for large scale optimization [accessed 2026-11-24]
Review scope / review_level: selected-primary-scope
Author-hosted PDF selected physical pages 3–5 (printed 2–4), rendered locally and visually inspected: limited storage, deletion of oldest correction, Eq. (2.1) inverse-BFGS, Algorithm 2.1 and Eq. (2.6) retained-update construction. No full-paper/proof/experiment or Section 4 scaling review. The selected original uses weak Wolfe; this study deliberately uses a separately specified strong-Wolfe line search. Current-gamma least-squares scaling is independently derived here, not attributed to unread text.
SciPy 1.14.1 line_search documentation [accessed 2026-11-24]
Review scope / review_level: selected-primary-scope
Signature, c1/c2, descent-direction requirement, returned failure None and evaluation counts. Cited textbook pages were not read.

Review scope / review_level: selected-primary-scope
Options gtol, norm, c1/c2, hess_inv0 and precision-loss notes; no claim of reading a BFGS original paper.

## Optimization, noise and regularization in the Bratu inverse problem — Noise, model discrepancy and finite gamma paths [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-inverse-optimization/
Coverage: reading

Two independent noise vectors are reused across scales and data contexts. Forty-two fixed fits separate finite-list gamma selection from fixed-gamma local covariance.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Gradient and quasi-Newton optimization
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
Select the largest admissible gamma using 1.05 times the realized noise norm only after the full gamma path qualifies. Incomplete paths and complete paths with no admissible gamma are distinct. Four-point L-curves are descriptive diagnostics.
Bratu nonlinear boundary-value problem
Bratu inference uses 31 interior nodes, five observations, W=I/5 and Sigma=sigma² I. Existing 1023-grid observations are reused without regeneration. Fixed sigma values are 1e-4/1e-3, seeds are 67001/67002 and the gamma list has five entries.
Problem figure
A saved validation figure for this execution example. Its conditions and acceptance scope are documented by this page’s checks.
Noise, model discrepancy and finite gamma paths
This problem’s code and validation status
Exact / reference solutions
References and checks for this execution

## Optimization, noise and regularization in the Bratu inverse problem — Noise, model discrepancy and finite gamma paths [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-inverse-optimization/
Coverage: reading

Gate final residuals, physical KKT conditions and completion for all 42 fits, the selection rule, and covariance/bias/model-shift response against explicit scalar 2x2 algebra, including symmetry and PSD.
Same-problem reference · Finite-grid numerical reference
Bratu references for finite gamma paths and local linear noise propagation
Ellipses are plug-in noise propagation for a local Gauss–Newton linear model with the selected gamma treated as fixed. They omit nonlinear residual Hessians and selection randomness and are not selection-conditional covariance, a posterior or a coverage guarantee. Continuous gamma paths and real data remain unverified.

## Optimization, noise and regularization in the Bratu inverse problem — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-inverse-optimization/#bratu-noise-regularization-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Bratu inference uses 31 interior nodes, five observations, W=I/5 and Sigma=sigma² I. Existing 1023-grid observations are reused without regeneration. Fixed sigma values are 1e-4/1e-3, seeds are 67001/67002 and the gamma list has five entries.

## Optimization, noise and regularization in the Bratu inverse problem — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-inverse-optimization/#bratu-noise-regularization-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Select the largest admissible gamma using 1.05 times the realized noise norm only after the full gamma path qualifies. Incomplete paths and complete paths with no admissible gamma are distinct. Four-point L-curves are descriptive diagnostics.
G=K^TWK+\gamma IC_\gamma=G^{-1}K^TW\Sigma WKG^{-T}\operatorname{bias}_\gamma=-\gamma G^{-1}(\theta_* -\theta_0)

## Optimization, noise and regularization in the Bratu inverse problem — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-inverse-optimization/#bratu-noise-regularization-references
Coverage: reading

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
Regularization Tools, Version 4.1 for Matlab 7.3 [accessed 2026-11-24]
Review scope / review_level: selected-primary-scope
Official author manual: selected text around Section 2.5 and Section 2.9; physical pages 20 and 37 (printed 18 and 35) rendered locally and visually inspected. L-curve residual/solution norm tradeoff and discrepancy equation (2.61) were read. Four-point chord curvature here is a finite-list diagnostic, not the manual spline/corner algorithm, a theorem of optimal regularization or coverage. Original software (1994) and later article (2007) are separate bibliographic works and were not read.
SciPy 1.14.1 curve_fit documentation [accessed 2026-11-24]
Review scope / review_level: selected-primary-scope
sigma/absolute_sigma and covariance interpretation sections. The penalized sandwich covariance in this study is derived independently; it is not presented as curve_fit output.
SciPy 1.14.1 least_squares documentation [accessed 2026-11-24]
Review scope / review_level: selected-primary-scope

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-inverse-optimization/#bratu-noise-regularization-references
Coverage: reading

Parameters, bounds, callable Jacobian, method-specific ftol/xtol/gtol and x_scale, max_nfev, returned status and Notes on LM and TRF. LM does not handle bounds and requires at least as many residual rows as variables; TRF supports bounds. MINPACK/STIR original papers were not read in this preparation.

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-lbm-annulus/#run-all
Coverage: reading

Run inside atlas-lbm-annulus-2026-11-24 from the ZIP. This command executes all 1 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output
Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

## Annular Couette control for curved-wall LBM — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-lbm-annulus/#lbm-annular-couette-control-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Three-point quadratic interpolation on the reflected characteristic: twointerior outgoing samples forq<.5,oneinterior incoming sample forq>.5,exacthalfway atq=.5. Record movingwall correction,actual force/torque andnonzero wallmass; nofloor ormassrepair.
u_\theta=Ar+B/r,\quad A=-U_iR_i/(R_o^2-R_i^2),\quad B=U_iR_iR_o^2/(R_o^2-R_i^2)p=\tfrac12A^2r^2+2AB\log r-\tfrac12B^2/r^2+C,\quad T_{inner}=-4\pi\rho\nu B

## LBM lid-driven cavity at Re100 — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-lbm-cavity/#lbm-cavity-re100-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Standard D2Q9equilibrium/BGK collision, nonperiodic link streaming and moving halfway reflection atq=.5. Sum actual population wall impulses without density repair/interior reset. Compile shipped C++17temporarily and call fromPython.
f_i^{eq}=w_i\rho[1+3c_i\cdot u+\frac92(c_i\cdot u)^2-\frac32|u|^2],\quad\nu_\ell=(\tau-1/2)/3f_{\bar i}(x,t+1)=f_i^\star(x,t)-6w_i\rho_0c_i\cdot u_w,\quad\rho_0=1\mathrm{Re}=UL/\nu=100,\quad t_\star=100

## Level sets: 2D circle translation and rigid rotation — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-level-set/#level-set-translation-assumptions
Coverage: reading

All quantities are nondimensional on[0,1]², with phi<0 inside. The prescribed divergence-free rigid motion keeps the circle away from the boundary. ## Level sets: 2D circle translation and rigid rotation — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-level-set/#level-set-translation-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Both modes use the same second-order ENO one-sided differences and Heun RK2, selecting stencils by absolute second differences. Optional redistancing occurs every.1 physical time: five first-order Godunov steps, dtau=.3dx, with the smoothed sign frozen per call. There is no volume correction, interface projection, phi clipping, hidden retry or analytic interior reset.
\Gamma(t)=\{\mathbf{x}:\phi(\mathbf{x},t)=0\},\quad \phi_t+\mathbf{u}\cdot\nabla\phi=0,\quad\phi_{\rm ref}(\mathbf{x},t)=\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{c}(t)\|-0.15\psi_\tau+S_\epsilon(\phi_0)(\|\nabla\psi\|-1)=0,\quad S_\epsilon(z)=z/\sqrt{z^2+\Delta x^2}E_\Gamma=\max_{t\in\{.25,.5,.75,1\}}\max_{\mathbf{z}\in Z_h(t)}\left|\|\mathbf{z}-\mathbf{c}(t)\|-r\right|,\quad E_A=\max_t\left|A_h(t)/(\pi r^2)-1\right|

## Level sets: 2D circle translation and rigid rotation — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-level-set/#level-set-translation-limits
Coverage: reading

Sampled radial error is not a Hausdorff distance. Observed order refines dx and dt together rather than isolating spatial order. Redistancing need not improve area or position; errors increase here even on the finest grid. No numerical VOF ranking, separate PDE engine, topology change, curvature flow, surface tension or two-phase Navier–Stokes validation is claimed. The two motions are conditions of one transported-circle-interface problem.

## Level sets: 2D circle translation and rigid rotation — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-level-set/#level-set-translation-references
Coverage: reading

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
S. Osher and J. A. Sethian (1988). Fronts propagating with curvature-dependent speed: Algorithms based on Hamilton-Jacobi formulations · DOI: 10.1016/0021-9991(88)90002-2
Review scope / review_level: full-text
Selected author-hosted original passages: abstract, implicit front representation and Hamilton–Jacobi transport/normal-motion formulation. No full-paper audit or reproduction of its full experiment suite.
C. W. Hirt and B. D. Nichols (1981). Volume of fluid (VOF) method for the dynamics of free boundaries · DOI: 10.1016/0021-9991(81)90145-5
Review scope / review_level: abstract-and-metadata
Publisher bibliography and abstract for the original volume-fraction formulation. No full-text algorithm audit or implementation of its donor–acceptor scheme.
M. Sussman and E. Fatemi (1999). An Efficient, Interface-Preserving Level Set Redistancing Algorithm and Its Application to Interfacial Incompressible Fluid Flow · DOI: 10.1137/S1064827596298245
Review scope / review_level: abstract-and-metadata

## Level sets: 2D circle translation and rigid rotation — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-level-set/#level-set-translation-references
Coverage: reading

Official abstract and bibliography: redistancing quality includes retaining the zero interface; its constrained higher-order algorithm is not the simple Godunov auxiliary iteration implemented here.
M. Sussman and E. G. Puckett (2000). A Coupled Level Set and Volume-of-Fluid Method for Computing 3D and Axisymmetric Incompressible Two-Phase Flows · DOI: 10.1006/jcph.2000.6537
Review scope / review_level: full-text
Author-hosted pp.302–305, equations(1)–(6),(9),(12),(15): signed-distance geometry, enclosed-mass issue and volume-fraction conservation. Sign is reversed here to make phi negative inside. No CLSVOF or two-phase fluid experiment executed.

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-level-set/
Coverage: reading

Rotate a radius.15 circle initially centered at(.68,.5) once about(.5,.5), with angular speed2pi. ENO2/Heun on32²/64²/128² grids compares optional redistancing, intermediate interfaces, geometric area and coupled grid/time refinement.

Both modes use the same second-order ENO one-sided differences and Heun RK2, selecting stencils by absolute second differences. Optional redistancing occurs every.1 physical time: five first-order Godunov steps, dtau=.3dx, with the smoothed sign frozen per call. There is no volume correction, interface projection, phi clipping, hidden retry or analytic interior reset.

## Level sets: 2D circle translation and rigid rotation — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-level-set/#level-set-rotation-assumptions
Coverage: reading

All quantities are nondimensional on[0,1]², with phi<0 inside. The prescribed divergence-free rigid motion keeps the circle away from the boundary. Two exterior ghost layers receive analytic data at each RK stage; this is not a periodic boundary. Every interior value is numerically advanced. Observe0/.25/.5/.75/1; max(|u|+|v|)dt/dx<=.35.

## Level sets: 2D circle translation and rigid rotation — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-level-set/#level-set-rotation-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Both modes use the same second-order ENO one-sided differences and Heun RK2, selecting stencils by absolute second differences. Optional redistancing occurs every.1 physical time: five first-order Godunov steps, dtau=.3dx, with the smoothed sign frozen per call. There is no volume correction, interface projection, phi clipping, hidden retry or analytic interior reset.
\Gamma(t)=\{\mathbf{x}:\phi(\mathbf{x},t)=0\},\quad \phi_t+\mathbf{u}\cdot\nabla\phi=0,\quad\phi_{\rm ref}(\mathbf{x},t)=\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{c}(t)\|-0.15\psi_\tau+S_\epsilon(\phi_0)(\|\nabla\psi\|-1)=0,\quad S_\epsilon(z)=z/\sqrt{z^2+\Delta x^2}E_\Gamma=\max_{t\in\{.25,.5,.75,1\}}\max_{\mathbf{z}\in Z_h(t)}\left|\|\mathbf{z}-\mathbf{c}(t)\|-r\right|,\quad E_A=\max_t\left|A_h(t)/(\pi r^2)-1\right|

## Level sets: 2D circle translation and rigid rotation — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-level-set/#level-set-rotation-validation
Coverage: reading

Analytic center motion and signed distance provide the reference. Take worst errors over the four positive common observation times. Interface error samples linearly interpolated grid-edge zeros; area comes from the negative portion of a piecewise-linear triangulation between grid centers, retaining initial geometric bias. Also record phi error and distance-gradient quality in|phi_exact|<=2dx, each redistancing area jump and a separateN64 CFL-halving sensitivity.

## Level sets: 2D circle translation and rigid rotation — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-level-set/#level-set-rotation-limits
Coverage: reading

Sampled radial error is not a Hausdorff distance. Observed order refines dx and dt together rather than isolating spatial order. Redistancing need not improve area or position; errors increase here even on the finest grid. No numerical VOF ranking, separate PDE engine, topology change, curvature flow, surface tension or two-phase Navier–Stokes validation is claimed. The two motions are conditions of one transported-circle-interface problem.

Coverage: reading

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
S. Osher and J. A. Sethian (1988). Fronts propagating with curvature-dependent speed: Algorithms based on Hamilton-Jacobi formulations · DOI: 10.1016/0021-9991(88)90002-2
Review scope / review_level: full-text
Selected author-hosted original passages: abstract, implicit front representation and Hamilton–Jacobi transport/normal-motion formulation. No full-paper audit or reproduction of its full experiment suite.
C. W. Hirt and B. D. Nichols (1981). Volume of fluid (VOF) method for the dynamics of free boundaries · DOI: 10.1016/0021-9991(81)90145-5
Review scope / review_level: abstract-and-metadata
Publisher bibliography and abstract for the original volume-fraction formulation. No full-text algorithm audit or implementation of its donor–acceptor scheme.
M. Sussman and E. Fatemi (1999). An Efficient, Interface-Preserving Level Set Redistancing Algorithm and Its Application to Interfacial Incompressible Fluid Flow · DOI: 10.1137/S1064827596298245
Review scope / review_level: abstract-and-metadata

## Level sets: 2D circle translation and rigid rotation — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-level-set/#level-set-rotation-references
Coverage: reading

Official abstract and bibliography: redistancing quality includes retaining the zero interface; its constrained higher-order algorithm is not the simple Godunov auxiliary iteration implemented here.
M. Sussman and E. G. Puckett (2000). A Coupled Level Set and Volume-of-Fluid Method for Computing 3D and Axisymmetric Incompressible Two-Phase Flows · DOI: 10.1006/jcph.2000.6537
Review scope / review_level: full-text
Author-hosted pp.302–305, equations(1)–(6),(9),(12),(15): signed-distance geometry, enclosed-mass issue and volume-fraction conservation. Sign is reversed here to make phi negative inside. No CLSVOF or two-phase fluid experiment executed.

Run inside atlas-linear-algebra-spectral-2026-11-24-r3 from the ZIP. This command executes all 4 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output

MINRES and GMRES use the same original-system residual criterion and are checked against the ideal Schur three-point spectrum.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Educational MINRES for symmetric-indefinite systems
Restarted GMRES
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
Stored-basis Lanczos least squares provides the educational MINRES variant; GMRES uses two-pass modified Gram-Schmidt. An SPD congruence preserves symmetry. The internal target is min(configured rtol, fixed forward-error limit / kappa_infinity), using only the matrix. The independent solution is not a stopping input.

Algebraic mixed-Poisson/Stokes-type blocks with velocity sizes 12 and 24 and pressure sizes 5 and 11. The common original-system residual tolerance is 1e-9.

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-linear-algebra-spectral/

Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Krylov eigenvalue solvers
Generalized eigenpairs with SciPy LOBPCG
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
Elementwise K and M assembly, M-inner-product Krylov iteration on K^-1 M, and actual SciPy LOBPCG with a small exact-K-inverse preconditioner. LOBPCG starts from {1, x^3, x^6}; degree-plus-two images avoid the structural rank defect of {1, x, x^2}. The same M is applied through a qualified einsum LinearOperator, avoiding the dense-B adapter. The eigensolver itself remains SciPy LOBPCG.
Fixed-end string eigenvalues and consistent-mass FEM
A unit string with unit tension and density and homogeneous Dirichlet endpoints. Use 15, 31 and 63 interior nodes and the lowest three eigenpairs.

## Linear algebra: factorizations, saddle systems, restarting and mass eigenpairs — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-linear-algebra-spectral/#fem-mass-eigen-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Elementwise K and M assembly, M-inner-product Krylov iteration on K^-1 M, and actual SciPy LOBPCG with a small exact-K-inverse preconditioner. LOBPCG starts from {1, x^3, x^6}; degree-plus-two images avoid the structural rank defect of {1, x, x^2}. The same M is applied through a qualified einsum LinearOperator, avoiding the dense-B adapter. The eigensolver itself remains SciPy LOBPCG.
K x=lambda M xlambda_j,h=6(1-cos(theta_j))/[h^2(2+cos(theta_j))]X^T M X=I

SciPy 1.14.1 LOBPCG API

Selected discussion of SPD B, preconditioner M, the history tuple, the 3k eigensolve, the 5k > n fallback and the rod example was read. This maintained-library comparison shares reduced LAPACK primitives; LOBPCG is not independently authored here.
