Selected _makeMatMat, _b_orthonormalize and API lines were read. The installed pinned file is bound separately. No full reading of the original LOBPCG paper or byte equality between wheel and Web source formatting is claimed.

## Low-Mach isentropic vortex: preconditioned Roe flux verification — Low-Mach isentropic vortex: preconditioned Roe flux verification [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-low-mach/
Coverage: reading

The same 2D Euler isentropic-vortex family is evolved at background Mach numbers .1 and .01 on 16², 32² and 64² grids to T=.1. Both Roe variants use unlimited central primitive-variable MUSCL reconstruction and SSPRK(3,3); one preconditions numerical dissipation with a Miczek-type matrix. Physical time and acoustic CFL=.2 are retained.

## Low-Mach isentropic vortex: preconditioned Roe flux verification — Low-Mach isentropic vortex: preconditioned Roe flux verification [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-low-mach/
Coverage: reading

Both finite-volume variants use the same unlimited centered primitive-MUSCL reconstruction, the physical Euler flux and SSPRK(3,3); only Roe dissipation is replaced by D=P^-1|PA|. At each Roe state use the total-speed Mach with mu=min(1,max(M_local,M_infinity)) and delta=1/mu-1, applying the primitive Miczek matrix through conserved-variable Jacobians. A degree-two characteristic polynomial applies the matrix absolute value; a separate dense eigendecomposition checks it. Physical time and sound speed are unchanged; acoustic CFL=0.2 remains. Reconstructed faces and all three stages check positive density and pressure, without limiters, floors, repair, hidden retries or pseudo-time iteration. A forward-Euler amplification counterexample prevents claiming SSP/TVD or general nonlinear stability from the integrator name.
Compressible Euler equations
Unforced 2D ideal-gas Euler is advanced in the original conservative variables and physical time. Fixed inputs use gamma=1.4, a periodic 20×20 box and a consistently scaled isentropic vortex with Mach-dependent background pressure.
Problem figure
A saved validation figure for this execution example. Its conditions and acceptance scope are documented by this page’s checks.

## Low-Mach isentropic vortex: preconditioned Roe flux verification — Low-Mach isentropic vortex: preconditioned Roe flux verification [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-low-mach/
Coverage: reading

The original 32 unit tests passed, but one of 143 first-order spatial gates failed: finest M_infinity=0.01 whole-domain dynamic pressure error 0.16537 exceeded the fixed 0.1 threshold. Original sources, contract, all twelve fields and the failed global pressure plot are retained. Revision 2 gives both fluxes the same unlimited centered primitive MUSCL and adds three checks for reconstruction, raw face failure and actual-RHS linearization against independent matrices. Inputs, physical time, CFL and acceptance bytes are unchanged; the revised 35-test/143-gate contract was frozen before revision execution. Checks cover Roe conserved jumps and physical-flux differences, dense-matrix dissipation, the three stages and raw invalid-stage retention. Each background Mach/flux has 17^2 constant-state Fourier modes and powers 1/10/100 in stated physical acoustic-energy variables. Pressure errors divide by rho_infinity*|U_infinity|^2 rather than the large p_infinity; velocity errors divide by analytic vortex perturbations. Initial R_h-q_t for the translating analytic field is retained as truncation error, not converged steady residual. Revision 2 passed all 35 tests, twelve runs and 143 gates with -W error, taking about 4.4 seconds on the original Mac. At finest M_infinity=0.01, relative velocity L1 was 0.07411 for Roe and 0.01847 for preconditioning; fixed-core pressure errors were 0.04871

## Low-Mach isentropic vortex: preconditioned Roe flux verification — Low-Mach isentropic vortex: preconditioned Roe flux verification [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-low-mach/
Coverage: reading

/0.0006325. Whole-domain pressure errors were instead 0.01194/0.01260, slightly worse with preconditioning; M_infinity=0.1 similarly gave 0.0006653/0.0006737. Maximum relative conserved-budget residual was 4.24e-14. Dynamic-scale Gauss8/16 maximum difference was 4.08e-11 and analytic Euler substitution residual 1.09e-16. Sampled SSPRK3 spectral radii and stated energy-scaled matrix powers had maximum 1. Forward Euler exceeded 1 for both MUSCL variants, reaching about 1.03560 for preconditioning at M_infinity=0.01.
Same-problem reference · Analytic reference
Isentropic vortex: analytic Euler field for low-Mach comparisons
Analytic field for the same translating isentropic-vortex family. Pressure and velocity are evaluated after Gauss integration of conserved variables; finite-periodic Gaussian tails and quadrature error remain explicit.

## Low-Mach isentropic vortex: preconditioned Roe flux verification — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-low-mach/#low-mach-vortex-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Periodic [-10,10]^2, gamma=1.4, beta=3, background density 1 and velocity (1,0.5). Set p_infinity=|U_infinity|^2/(gamma M_infinity^2), retaining the same flow and vortex strengths. Background Mach is not maximum local Mach. A whole-plane translating isentropic vortex is evaluated with minimum-image coordinates and a separately qualified Gaussian seam. Conserved cell means use eight-point tensor Gauss quadrature, checked against order 16; they are not closed-form exact means or a generic exactly periodic nonlinear vortex.

## Low-Mach isentropic vortex: preconditioned Roe flux verification — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-low-mach/#low-mach-vortex-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Both finite-volume variants use the same unlimited centered primitive-MUSCL reconstruction, the physical Euler flux and SSPRK(3,3); only Roe dissipation is replaced by D=P^-1|PA|. At each Roe state use the total-speed Mach with mu=min(1,max(M_local,M_infinity)) and delta=1/mu-1, applying the primitive Miczek matrix through conserved-variable Jacobians. A degree-two characteristic polynomial applies the matrix absolute value; a separate dense eigendecomposition checks it. Physical time and sound speed are unchanged; acoustic CFL=0.2 remains. Reconstructed faces and all three stages check positive density and pressure, without limiters, floors, repair, hidden retries or pseudo-time iteration. A forward-Euler amplification counterexample prevents claiming SSP/TVD or general nonlinear stability from the integrator name.
\partial_tU+\partial_xF(U)+\partial_yG(U)=0,\quad U=(\rho,\rho u,\rho v,E)^T\widehat F=\tfrac12(F_L+F_R)-\tfrac12J P^{-1}|P A|J^{-1}(U_R-U_L),\quad \mu=\min(1,\max(M_{\rm local},M_\infty)),\quad\delta=\mu^{-1}-1p_\infty=\frac{|U_\infty|^2}{\gamma M_\infty^2},\qquad \Delta t=\frac{0.2\Delta x}{\max(|u|+c)+\max(|v|+c)}\chi(k)=\sin k\,(3-\cos k)/2,\quad\psi(k)=(1-\cos k)^2/2,\quad L_h=-i\sum_j\chi(k_j\Delta x)A_j/\Delta x-\sum_j\psi(k_j\Delta x)D_j/\Delta x,\quad R(z)=I+z+z^2/2+z^3/6

## Low-Mach isentropic vortex: preconditioned Roe flux verification — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-low-mach/#low-mach-vortex-limits
Coverage: reading

This is a short T=0.1 fixed-input, few-grid test, not a full circulation or long-time preservation study. The Fourier check covers selected uniform states, wave numbers and powers; it is no proof for all modes, nonlinear variable states or general positivity. Actual integration retains the acoustic CFL and does not use the displayed convective diagnostic step. Steady convergence acceleration, dual time, shock/contact robustness, general meshes and all Mach numbers remain unverified. Finite periodic-box seams, Gauss quadrature and primitive variables evaluated from cell means remain distinct qualifications. Pressure Mach dependence and local errors are retained. Unlimited MUSCL is selected for these smooth inputs, not a limiter, TVD method or general positivity guarantee. The original box-wide pressure waves are shown in a separate full-domain failed-trial figure rather than hidden by the gallery core crop. Velocity/core improvements do not imply globally better pressure: finest whole-domain pressure L1 is slightly larger with preconditioning and grows when background Mach is reduced by ten. No Mach-independent pressure accuracy follows from these measurements. Perturbation kinetic energy is a diagnostic computed from conserved cell means, not exact conservation of continuous kinetic energy.

## Low-Mach isentropic vortex: preconditioned Roe flux verification — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-low-mach/#low-mach-vortex-references
Coverage: reading

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
Fabian Miczek, Friedrich K. Röpke and Philipp V. F. Edelmann (2015). New numerical solver for flows at various Mach numbers [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.1051/0004-6361/201425059
Review scope / review_level: selected-author-version-full-text: Section8 Eq56; Section4 explicit-RK3 discussion; AppendixA variable transforms; Section6 smooth piecewise-linear reconstruction without a limiter
Selected author-version equations and RK3 discussion were checked. This short isentropic-vortex application does not reproduce the paper’s Gresho or implicit-integration experiments. Section 6 also motivates unlimited piecewise-linear reconstruction for smooth tests; this is independent motivation for the revision.
Wasilij Barsukow, Philipp V. F. Edelmann, Christian Klingenberg, Fabian Miczek and Friedrich K. Röpke (2017). A Numerical Scheme for the Compressible Low-Mach Number Regime of Ideal Fluid Dynamics [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.1007/s10915-017-0372-4
Review scope / review_level: selected-full-text: Section3 Eqs21,31,32; Section5 Eq83 and Fourier-mode stability discussion

Coverage: reading

Checked the modified dissipation, primitive matrix and restrictive forward-Euler stability result. The present SSPRK33 Fourier/stage checks are separate fixed-input evidence, not a general nonlinear or SSP guarantee.
Seth C. Spiegel, H. T. Huynh and James R. DeBonis (2015). A Survey of the Isentropic Euler Vortex Problem using High-Order Methods [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.2514/6.2015-2444
Review scope / review_level: selected-primary-report: parameterized vortex definitions and Sections IV.B/IV.C boundary discussion
Checked the generalized vortex and finite-periodic-boundary qualifications. The selected beta3, mean velocity(1,.5) and background Mach values are explicit adaptations, not NASA/FR execution or figure reuse.
Sigal Gottlieb and Chi-Wang Shu (1998). Total Variation Diminishing Runge-Kutta Schemes [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.1090/S0025-5718-98-00913-2

## Mie scattering width of a two-dimensional dielectric cylinder — Mie scattering width of a two-dimensional dielectric cylinder [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-maxwell-cylinder/
Coverage: reading

Use 12/18/24 points per wavelength, 32 burn-in periods and 8 measured periods. Check two contours, consecutive four-period windows, half-amplitude phasors after a complete repeated evolution, and a vacuum control at the five saved times. Compare scattering width and exterior fields with the cylindrical series.
Same-problem reference · Analytic reference
Exterior series and scattering width of a dielectric cylinder
This is a lossless two-dimensional Ez cylinder, not a three-dimensional sphere. Report staircase geometry error without claiming general second-order curved-boundary accuracy or precision scattering for arbitrary frequencies and materials.

## Mie scattering width of a two-dimensional dielectric cylinder — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-maxwell-cylinder/#cylinder-mie2d-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Advance the scattered Yee fields with an exact discrete incident difference on the polarization-contrast support. Accumulate E and H at their own integer and half times, then integrate physical power after four-point native-face collocation.
\varepsilon\partial_tE_z=\partial_xH_y-\partial_yH_x,\quad\partial_tH_x=-\partial_yE_z,\quad\partial_tH_y=\partial_xE_z\Sigma_{\mathrm{sca}}=\frac4k\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}|a_n|^2,\quad\Sigma_{\mathrm{ext}}=-\frac4k\sum_n\operatorname{Re}a_n

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-maxwell-grazing/
Coverage: reading

Use five long trajectories: three joint grid/layer-strength resolutions, a normal control and a weakly damped companion. Reuse the byte-bound no-PML reference only after checking every unchanged reference argument. Retain the old 13 test bodies and add two parameter-policy/peak-12 work regressions; all original 44 long-trajectory gates remain unchanged.
Same-problem reference · Finite-grid numerical reference
Isolated same-grid reference for a long grazing dispersive packet
The central angle is 80 degrees; finite kx bandwidth gives neighboring angles. The no-PML reference shares the discretization and initialization to isolate boundary error from bulk dispersion. Small operator and finite-trajectory checks do not prove global stability for arbitrary angles and materials. The joint family does not measure fixed-PML spatial order; the older 100 checks alone do not prove peak-12 global stability.

## Long-time grazing PML in a dispersive medium — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-maxwell-grazing/#dispersive-grazing-pml-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Use c = 1 and a homogeneous Lorentz medium with epsilon_inf = 1, delta_epsilon = 0.2 and omega_0 = 12 continuing through the PML. Joint refinement uses 512/768/1024 cells and peaks 6/9/12. The normal coarse control has peak 6; the damped fine companion has peak 12. Length 64, layer thickness 12, center 32, width 4 and carrier 6 are fixed.

## Long-time grazing PML in a dispersive medium — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-maxwell-grazing/#dispersive-grazing-pml-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Couple Yee and midpoint ADE updates to a trapezoidal derivative-memory filter at native times. Separate positive physical dissipation from signed numerical PML work, retaining all physical and auxiliary states.
\partial_t\psi=-s_x(\psi+D_xu),\quad D_x^{\mathrm{PML}}u=D_xu+\psi\psi^n=b\psi^{n-1}+c(D^n+D^{n-1}),\quad b=\frac{1-s_x\Delta t/2}{1+s_x\Delta t/2},\quad c=\frac{-s_x\Delta t/2}{1+s_x\Delta t/2}\Delta\mathcal E_{\mathrm{mod}}+W_{\mathrm{physical}}-W_{\mathrm{PML}}=0

## Oblique s/p incidence on a Lorentz-dispersive slab — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-maxwell-lorentz/#lorentz-oblique-sp-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Use the single-ky Yee spatial operator and local implicit-midpoint Lorentz ADE. Couple both p-polarized electric components to polarization, and remove incident propagation with a matched vacuum pulse on the same grid. Accumulate direct Ohmic and material-damping work separately from modified energy.
\varepsilon_\infty\partial_t\mathbf E=\nabla\times\mathbf H-\sigma\mathbf E-\mathbf J,\quad\partial_t\mathbf P=\mathbf J\partial_t\mathbf J=f\mathbf E-\omega_0^2\mathbf P-\gamma\mathbf J,\quad f=\Delta\varepsilon\omega_0^2\varepsilon(\omega)=\varepsilon_\infty+\frac{f}{\omega_0^2-\omega^2-i\gamma\omega}+\frac{i\sigma}{\omega}

Read Material Dispersion, Numerical Stability, Loss and Gain, and Conductivity. Confirmed the exp(-i omega t) convention, Lorentz polarization and dispersive-PML warning. ## Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics — Multimodal MCMC: trapping, false reassurance and a global proposal [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mcmc/
Coverage: reading

Compare with analytic moments, seven declared CDF points and positive occupancy. Record per-chain occupancies/transitions, rank/folded split Rhat, bulk/tail/mean and mode-indicator ESS, and within-only ACF/ESS. Dispersed trapped chains can have a good pooled distribution yet fail between-chain diagnostics; same-mode chains can have reassuring Rhat yet fail the known target. A control scenario passes when its intended failure is detected. CDF error is a declared-point maximum, not whole-line KS distance or an IID-test p-value.
No corresponding reference-library card is registered. The execution-specific validation material above documents its reference values and acceptance checks.

## Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mcmc/#mcmc-multimodal-mixing-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Dimensionless1D target p=.5N(−6,1)+.5N(6,1), mean0/variance37/positive occupancy.5. Three fixed seeds, four chains,1024 warmup and16384 retained draws/chain. Prefixes1024/4096/16384 are nested, not independent replications. Rejections/self-transitions are retained.

## Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mcmc/#mcmc-multimodal-mixing-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Local scale.8; mixed uses y=−x+.8Z with probability.1, otherwise y=x+.8Z. The state-independent mixture is symmetric q(y|x)=q(x|y), so MH uses the log-target ratio. Chains use independent PCG64 streams, with no adaptation or removal of rejected states.
\pi(x)=\tfrac12\phi(x+6)+\tfrac12\phi(x-6),\quad E[X]=0,\quad\operatorname{Var}X=37F(x)=\tfrac12\Phi(x+6)+\tfrac12\Phi(x-6),\quad P(X>0)=\tfrac12q(y\mid x)=(1-p)\phi_s(y-x)+p\phi_s(y+x)=q(x\mid y),\quad s=.8,\ p=.1\alpha(x,y)=\min\{1,\pi(y)/\pi(x)\},\quad I_n=\mathbf1\{X_n>0\}

## Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mcmc/#mcmc-multimodal-mixing-validation
Coverage: reading

Compare with analytic moments, seven declared CDF points and positive occupancy. Record per-chain occupancies/transitions, rank/folded split Rhat, bulk/tail/mean and mode-indicator ESS, and within-only ACF/ESS. Dispersed trapped chains can have a good pooled distribution yet fail between-chain diagnostics; same-mode chains can have reassuring Rhat yet fail the known target. A control scenario passes when its intended failure is detected. CDF error is a declared-point maximum, not whole-line KS distance or an IID-test p-value.

## Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mcmc/#mcmc-multimodal-mixing-limits
Coverage: reading

An educational fixed-seed, finite-budget experiment. The local Gaussian RW is theoretically irreducible MH; finite-time trapping is not called a nonergodic algorithm. Small Rhat, large ESS and pooled-CDF agreement cannot rule out undiscovered modes. Symmetry-informed reflection is not a generic multimodal solver. No quantum calculations.

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mcmc/#mcmc-multimodal-mixing-references
Coverage: reading

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
A. Vehtari, A. Gelman, D. Simpson, B. Carpenter and P.-C. Bürkner (2021). Rank-Normalization, Folding, and Localization: An Improved R-hat for Assessing Convergence of MCMC (with Discussion) · DOI: 10.1214/20-BA1221
Review scope / review_level: corrected-author-paper-selected-sections
Checked original sections3–4, the2021-06-22 correction of Eq4.1 to denominator S+1/4, and the constant-indicator warning. This does not reproduce every original numerical experiment.
C. J. Geyer (1992). Practical Markov Chain Monte Carlo · DOI: 10.1214/ss/1177011137
Review scope / review_level: original-selected-paired-sequence-theory
Checked section3.3 and Theorems3.1/3.2 for reversibility assumptions and initial-positive/monotone sequences. Main article pp473–483 are distinguished from combined discussion pagination; no claim gives exact true ESS from finite chains.
A. Gelman and D. B. Rubin (1992). Inference from Iterative Simulation Using Multiple Sequences · DOI: 10.1214/ss/1177011136
Review scope / review_level: original-selected-multiple-chain-starting-points

## Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mcmc/#mcmc-multimodal-mixing-references
Coverage: reading

Checked the original introduction/section2 on multiple sequences and overdispersed starts. Distinct from the later rank/folded method, and not a reproduction of every1992 finite-sample correction.
The ArviZ developers (2024). ArviZ0.20.0 public diagnostics API and tagged source
Review scope / review_level: official-versioned-source-and-actual-independent-execution
Checked the official0.20.0 rhat/ess API and tagged source for splitting, ranks, Type7 quantiles, endpoints and constant conventions. Installed source hashes match commit94113176cae99a05ba41d1e93739ee2d5bdbe9b1;62 byte-identical datasets were actually processed in a separate environment without importing Atlas diagnostics. No upstream implementation is reproduced; values, versions, hashes and regeneration code are supplied.
N. Metropolis, A. W. Rosenbluth, M. N. Rosenbluth, A. H. Teller and E. Teller (1953). Equation of State Calculations by Fast Computing Machines · DOI: 10.1063/1.1699114
Review scope / review_level: publisher-abstract-and-metadata
Publisher bibliography and abstract checked. Cited for symmetric-proposal Metropolis acceptance; no reproduction of the original hard-sphere experiment is claimed.
W. K. Hastings (1970). Monte Carlo sampling methods using Markov chains and their applications · DOI: 10.1093/biomet/57.1.97
Review scope / review_level: original-paper-excerpt-and-metadata

## Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics — Independent MCMC diagnostic checks: rank Rhat, bulk/tail ESS and degeneracies [en]

Actually process62 byte-identical datasets with separately installed ArviZ0.20.0, bound by recipe/input/chain/official-source hashes. Separate finite-value agreement from explicit degeneracy-policy differences.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Markov-chain Monte Carlo / MCMC
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s diagnostic and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
Original equation-based implementation: split with the odd center dropped, average-tie Blom ranks using corrected S+1/4, re-rank folded deviations, and take the larger Rhat. Bulk ESS uses rank-split draws; tail ESS first determines Type7 quantiles on original full draws, then splits <= indicators. Use initial-positive/monotone pairs, declared endpoint handling and tau>=1/log10(total), without clipping antithetic ESS to N.

## Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics — Independent MCMC diagnostic checks: rank Rhat, bulk/tail ESS and degeneracies [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mcmc/
Coverage: reading

References and checks for this execution
Reference and validation scope
62 datasets: nine actual chains times three prefixes times x/indicator plus eight small fixtures. Regenerate and hash identical bytes; compare ordinary finite Rhat/ESS/ACF and test constants, zero within-chain variance, odd lengths, ties, shift and scale. Direct lag sums and infinite-series stationary-AR(1) tau=(1+rho)/(1−rho) provide separate checks of finite estimates. Routine runs compare stored references; live ArviZ regeneration is a separate optional procedure.
No corresponding reference-library card is registered. The execution-specific validation material above documents its reference values and acceptance checks.

## Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mcmc/#mcmc-diagnostic-reference-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Dimensionless1D target p=.5N(−6,1)+.5N(6,1), mean0/variance37/positive occupancy.5. Three fixed seeds, four chains,1024 warmup and16384 retained draws/chain. Prefixes1024/4096/16384 are nested, not independent replications. Rejections/self-transitions are retained.

## Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mcmc/#mcmc-diagnostic-reference-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Original equation-based implementation: split with the odd center dropped, average-tie Blom ranks using corrected S+1/4, re-rank folded deviations, and take the larger Rhat. Bulk ESS uses rank-split draws; tail ESS first determines Type7 quantiles on original full draws, then splits <= indicators. Use initial-positive/monotone pairs, declared endpoint handling and tau>=1/log10(total), without clipping antithetic ESS to N.
\widehat R=\sqrt{\widehat V^+/W},\quad\widehat V^+=\tfrac{N-1}{N}W+\tfrac BNz_s=\Phi^{-1}\!\left(\frac{r_s-3/8}{S+1/4}\right),\quad\widehat R_{\rm rank}=\max(\widehat R_z,\widehat R_{\rm folded})\widehat N_{\rm eff}=MN/\widehat\tau,\quad\widehat\tau=-1+2\sum_k\widehat P_k,\quad\widehat P_k=\widehat\rho_{2k}+\widehat\rho_{2k+1}\operatorname{ESS}_{\rm tail}=\min\{\operatorname{ESS}(\mathbf1[X\le q_{.05}]),\operatorname{ESS}(\mathbf1[X\le q_{.95}])\}

## Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mcmc/#mcmc-diagnostic-reference-validation
Coverage: reading

62 datasets: nine actual chains times three prefixes times x/indicator plus eight small fixtures. Regenerate and hash identical bytes; compare ordinary finite Rhat/ESS/ACF and test constants, zero within-chain variance, odd lengths, ties, shift and scale. Direct lag sums and infinite-series stationary-AR(1) tau=(1+rho)/(1−rho) provide separate checks of finite estimates. Routine runs compare stored references; live ArviZ regeneration is a separate optional procedure.

## Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mcmc/#mcmc-diagnostic-reference-limits
Coverage: reading

An educational fixed-seed, finite-budget experiment. The local Gaussian RW is theoretically irreducible MH; finite-time trapping is not called a nonergodic algorithm. Small Rhat, large ESS and pooled-CDF agreement cannot rule out undiscovered modes. Symmetry-informed reflection is not a generic multimodal solver. No quantum calculations. ArviZ raw constant-ESS=N is not evidence of mixing. Globally identical values yield null/status; differing per-chain constants yield null/infinite-separation Rhat while retaining raw huge-finite/infinite library values outside ordinary finite comparisons. Bulk ESS is not a raw-mean MCSE estimator.

## Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mcmc/#mcmc-diagnostic-reference-references
Coverage: reading

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
A. Vehtari, A. Gelman, D. Simpson, B. Carpenter and P.-C. Bürkner (2021). Rank-Normalization, Folding, and Localization: An Improved R-hat for Assessing Convergence of MCMC (with Discussion) · DOI: 10.1214/20-BA1221
Review scope / review_level: corrected-author-paper-selected-sections
Checked original sections3–4, the2021-06-22 correction of Eq4.1 to denominator S+1/4, and the constant-indicator warning. This does not reproduce every original numerical experiment.
C. J. Geyer (1992). Practical Markov Chain Monte Carlo · DOI: 10.1214/ss/1177011137
Review scope / review_level: original-selected-paired-sequence-theory
Checked section3.3 and Theorems3.1/3.2 for reversibility assumptions and initial-positive/monotone sequences. Main article pp473–483 are distinguished from combined discussion pagination; no claim gives exact true ESS from finite chains.
A. Gelman and D. B. Rubin (1992). Inference from Iterative Simulation Using Multiple Sequences · DOI: 10.1214/ss/1177011136
Review scope / review_level: original-selected-multiple-chain-starting-points

## Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mcmc/#mcmc-diagnostic-reference-references
Coverage: reading

Checked the original introduction/section2 on multiple sequences and overdispersed starts. Distinct from the later rank/folded method, and not a reproduction of every1992 finite-sample correction.
The ArviZ developers (2024). ArviZ0.20.0 public diagnostics API and tagged source
Review scope / review_level: official-versioned-source-and-actual-independent-execution
Checked the official0.20.0 rhat/ess API and tagged source for splitting, ranks, Type7 quantiles, endpoints and constant conventions. Installed source hashes match commit94113176cae99a05ba41d1e93739ee2d5bdbe9b1;62 byte-identical datasets were actually processed in a separate environment without importing Atlas diagnostics. No upstream implementation is reproduced; values, versions, hashes and regeneration code are supplied.

## Corner singularities, curved coordinates and Neumann/Robin boundaries — Corner singularities, curved coordinates and Neumann/Robin boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mesh-boundary/
Coverage: reading

Actually solve singular L-corner P1 FEM, annular variable-viscosity vector Q1 PDE, pure-Neumann compatibility/mean-gauge and mixed-Robin manufactured problems.

## Corner singularities, curved coordinates and Neumann/Robin boundaries — Download and execute the supplement [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mesh-boundary/#run-all
Coverage: reading

Run inside atlas-mesh-boundary-2026-11-23 from the ZIP. This command executes all 4 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output

## CT and GLM: matched controls, independent checks and grid/time convergence — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mhd-convergence/#ct-glm-smooth-convergence-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Periodic unit square, gamma5/3, mu0=1, planar MHD. A=.05[cos2pi(x−.3t)+cos2pi(y−.2t)], B=(Ay,−Ax), rho1, v=(.3,.2), p=.1+(2pi)²A²/2 at t=.1. Compare analytic conserved cell averages. This is a constructed verification case, not a claimed published standard benchmark.

## CT and GLM: matched controls, independent checks and grid/time convergence — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mhd-convergence/#ct-glm-smooth-convergence-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Both use piecewise constants, the same fixed Rusanov speed alpha3 and forward Euler. CT uses face B/shared arithmetic corner EMFs; GLM uses cell B/psi with fixed ch3 and physical damping rate kappa2. All meshes use384 steps and identical CT/GLM dt sequences; initial reconstructed CT cell B matches GLM cell B.
A=a[\cos k(x-ut)+\cos k(y-vt)],\quad\mathbf B=(A_y,-A_x),\quad J_z=-\Delta A=k^2Ap=p_0+\tfrac12k^2A^2,\qquad\nabla p=J_z\nabla A=\mathbf J\times\mathbf B\bar{\mathbf U}_{ij}=\frac1{\Delta x\Delta y}\int_{K_{ij}}\mathbf U\,dx\,dy,\qquad p(\bar{\mathbf U})\ne\bar p\mathbf U^{m+1}=\mathbf U^m+\Delta t\,L_h(\mathbf U^m),\qquad C_{\rm sum}=\alpha\Delta t(\Delta x^{-1}+\Delta y^{-1})

## CT and GLM: matched controls, independent checks and grid/time convergence — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mhd-convergence/#ct-glm-smooth-convergence-validation
Coverage: reading

Measure conserved-variable L1/L2/Linf errors and observed orders at16²/32²/64². Compare finest-grid step doubling with.1 of the spatial error. At fixed8², compare16/32/64/128 steps with doubly refined DOP853 tolerances/max steps. Record mass/E, positivity, native CT divergence, common cell divergence and psi.

## CT and GLM: matched controls, independent checks and grid/time convergence — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mhd-convergence/#ct-glm-smooth-convergence-limits
Coverage: reading

With constant LLF viscosity and periodic centered operators, the GLM div=psi=0 subspace remains invariant up to roundoff. This tests coupled-MHD accuracy; a separate nonphysical control activates cleaning. p(q-average) is not the exact averaged p. DOP853 is independent in time only and shares the spatial RHS. Step differences are empirical contamination indicators, not rigorous bounds; face/cell representation differences remain part of the comparison.

## CT and GLM: matched controls, independent checks and grid/time convergence — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mhd-convergence/#ct-glm-ot-convergence-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Standard periodic OT: gamma5/3, rho25/(36pi), p5/(12pi), v=(−sin2piy,sin2pix), B=(−sin2piy,sin4pix)/sqrt(4pi), t=.05. Both methods share192 steps on16²/32²/64². This supplements the previous immutable release.

## CT and GLM: matched controls, independent checks and grid/time convergence — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mhd-convergence/#ct-glm-ot-convergence-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Primary runs use fixed alpha=ch=3 Rusanov/forward Euler and grid-independent GLM kappa2. Independent C++ Athena++ uses HLLD/PLM/RK2/upwind CT. Continuous initial fields agree; Athena’s face/primitive discretization is not identical.
F_{i+1/2}=\tfrac12[F(U_L)+F(U_R)-\alpha(U_R-U_L)],\qquad\alpha=3(B_x)_t+\partial_x\psi+\partial_y(v_yB_x-v_xB_y)=0,\quad\psi_t+c_h^2\nabla\cdot\mathbf B=-\kappa\psiD_h^{\rm face}\,\operatorname{curl}_h E=0,\qquad D_h^{\rm cell}\ne D_h^{\rm face}

## CT and GLM: matched controls, independent checks and grid/time convergence — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mhd-convergence/#ct-glm-ot-convergence-validation
Coverage: reading

Measure density/magnetic L1 error, mesh improvement, positivity, conservation and div/psi. Athena256²/512² both useCFL.15; fixed512² CFL.3/.15 checks reference time sensitivity, with increments compared against.1 of primary error. At fixed16², compare primary time refinement with separately executed DOP853 and check finest-grid step doubling.

## CT and GLM: matched controls, independent checks and grid/time convergence — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mhd-convergence/#ct-glm-ot-convergence-limits
Coverage: reading

Short smooth OT, not certification of post-shock,3D or general cleaning behavior. Athena is a finite-grid numerical reference; increments are not error bounds. Historical128²/CFL.3 is not paired with256²/CFL.15 to infer a pure spatial order. Constant-LLF preservation of GLM div=psi=0 is not evidence of active cleaning. Native face and common centered divergences differ; centered checkerboard blind spots remain.

## CT and GLM: matched controls, independent checks and grid/time convergence — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mhd-convergence/#ct-glm-constraint-control-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Periodic32² grid,t=.1,128 steps,rho=p=1,v=0,By=psi=0. CT faceBx=.01cos[2pi(i+1)/32]; GLM cellBx equals the adjacent-face average. The intentional nonzero native CT divergence violates valid physical CT initial data and is treated solely as a diagnostic.

## CT and GLM: matched controls, independent checks and grid/time convergence — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mhd-convergence/#ct-glm-constraint-control-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Use the same fully coupled MHD code. With y-invariance andBy=vy=0, the GLM Bx/psi subsystem decouples from fluid feedback, allowing a separately constructed2x2 discrete Fourier symbol and forward-Euler matrix power. Compare kappa2/0 at identical dt and LLF viscosity, separating B/psi phase exchange from physical damping.
\widehat{U}^{m+1}=(I+\Delta t M_h)\widehat{U}^{m},\quad M_h=\begin{pmatrix}\nu_h&-i\widetilde{k}\\-ic_h^2\widetilde{k}&\nu_h-\kappa\end{pmatrix}\nu_h=\alpha N[\cos(2\pi/N)-1],\quad\widetilde{k}=N\sin(2\pi/N)W=\langle B_x^2+\psi^2/c_h^2\rangle,\qquad W_{\kappa=2}/W_{\kappa=0}<0.95

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mhd-convergence/#ct-glm-constraint-control-validation
Coverage: reading

Check preservation of the initial CT defect, nonzero GLM psi, independent FE agreement for bothBx/psi, positive density/pressure, and conserved physical E/mass. ## CT and GLM: matched controls, independent checks and grid/time convergence — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mhd-convergence/#ct-glm-constraint-control-limits
Coverage: reading

Passing means correctly detecting expected CT non-removal and the calibrated GLM response, not recommending non-solenoidal CT physical initial data. W is an auxiliary diagnostic norm, distinct from conserved physical total energy E without psi. B decay includes phase exchange and LLF diffusion; damping is assessed with the kappa0 control. No general nonlinear,boundary or shock cleaning guarantee is claimed.

## Independent MHD transport, waves and compression comparisons — Download and execute the supplement [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mhd-transport/#run-all
Coverage: reading

Run inside atlas-mhd-transport-2026-11-24 from the ZIP. This command executes all 3 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output
Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

## Independent MHD transport, waves and compression comparisons — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mhd-transport/#circular-alfven-refinement-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Full-eight-state HLLD fluxes, MC-MUSCL reconstruction and fixed-step Heun. One-dimensional finite-volume update with constant Bx.
\partial_tU+\partial_xF_x(U)=0,\quad U=(\rho,\rho\mathbf v,E,\mathbf B),\quad\gamma=5/3\theta_i=2\pi(x_i-t),\quad(\bar B_y,\bar B_z)=.1\frac{\sin(\pi h)}{\pi h}(\cos\theta_i,\sin\theta_i)\bar\rho=1,\quad\bar B_x=1,\quad(\bar m_y,\bar m_z)=-(\bar B_y,\bar B_z),\quad\bar E=.66e_2=\frac{\|U-U^{\mathrm{exact}}\|_2}{\|U^{\mathrm{exact}}\|_2},\qquad p_{\mathrm{obs}}=\log_2(e_h/e_{h/2})

## Independent MHD transport, waves and compression comparisons — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mhd-transport/#magnetic-loop-independent-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Full-eight-state HLLD fluxes, MC-MUSCL reconstruction and fixed-step Heun. Shared face fluxes and CT-contact corner EMFs update native face B; cell B is adjacent-face averaged. Initial discrete vector-potential curl and sampled fluid states match the official generator.
\partial_tU+\partial_xF_x(U)+\partial_yF_y(U)=0,\quad U=(\rho,\rho\mathbf v,E,\mathbf B)E=\frac{p}{\gamma-1}+\frac12\rho|\mathbf v|^2+\frac12|\mathbf B|^2,\quad\gamma=5/3\frac{dB_x}{dt}=-D_y\mathcal E_z,\quad\frac{dB_y}{dt}=D_x\mathcal E_z,\quad D_xB_x+D_yB_y=\mathrm{constant}\bar U_i^{\mathrm{ref}}=\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j\in i}\bar U_j^{\mathrm{fine}},\qquad e_1=\frac{\sum|U-U^{\mathrm{ref}}|}{\sum|U^{\mathrm{ref}}|}A_z=.001\max(.3-\sqrt{x^2+y^2},0),\qquad\mathbf v=(2,1,2)

## Independent MHD transport, waves and compression comparisons — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mhd-transport/#magnetic-loop-independent-limits
Coverage: reading

Educational fixed inputs only. Count HLLD-to-HLLE fallbacks and face reconstruction positivity scaling; no cell floor/clipping/retry. Finite-grid references are not exact solutions; no universal stability, positivity or order guarantee. Independent comparisons are final-only. Intermediate Athena outputs occur just after requested quarter times and are not matched frames. Athena native-face divergence is not exported/measured. Density contrast diagnoses compression, not a mathematical proof of shock formation.

Athena++ collaboration (2026). Athena++ official field_loop and orszag_tang problem generators, pinned source [accessed 2026-11-23]
Review scope / review_level: Official archive SHA verified; selected src/pgen/field_loop.cpp and orszag_tang.cpp, PLM/RK2/output configuration and actual conserved tab headers inspected; not a full Athena code audit

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-mhd/

Compare a longitudinal magnetic Fourier mode of GLM cleaning with the continuous linear matrix-exponential solution.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
GLM divergence cleaning
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations

Compare linear numerical fields with SciPy expm of continuum J-k²D and measure spatial convergence. Quantify the nonlinear run against a semidiscrete linear matrix exponential as a small-amplitude check, not validation of mature morphology.

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#turing-schnakenberg-references
Coverage: reading

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
A. M. Turing (1952). The Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis · DOI: 10.1098/rstb.1952.0012
Review scope / review_level: publisher-archive-and-original-first-page-metadata
Royal Society manuscript-review archive and bibliography on the original first page hosted by a university checked. Publisher text returned 403. Historical source for diffusion-driven instability, distinct from this adopted Schnakenberg example.
J. Schnakenberg (1979). Simple chemical reaction systems with limit cycle behaviour · DOI: 10.1016/0022-5193(79)90042-0
Review scope / review_level: official-bibliographic-metadata
PubMed bibliography and DOI checked (no abstract). Cited for the reaction-system family; a=0.1,b=0.9 and this spatial experiment are adopted educational inputs, not a transcription of the original experiment.
The SciPy community (2024). SciPy1.14.1 expm reference
Review scope / review_level: official-api-documentation
Official matrix-exponential API and description of the Pade/scaling-and-squaring method checked.

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — FitzHugh-Nagumo: pulse excitation, recovery and an independent ODE reference [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/
Coverage: reading

Excite a two-variable reduced membrane ODE with a current pulse; check all-output-time errors, temporal refinement and recovery against DOP853.

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#fitzhugh-nagumo-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Dimensionless a=0.7,b=0.8,tau=12.5. Start at resting equilibrium for I=0, apply I=0.8 only during t=10..20 and integrate to t=80. No calibration to physiological physical units.

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#fitzhugh-nagumo-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Use original RK4 with steps 0.1/0.05/0.025, splitting time intervals exactly at pulse discontinuities. At output spacing 0.1, measure the peak and distance from rest.
\dot v=v-v^3/3-w+I(t),\qquad \dot w=(v+a-bw)/\tau

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#fitzhugh-nagumo-validation
Coverage: reading

Compare separate SciPy DOP853 at rtol=1e-11 and 1e-13 to check reference sensitivity; measure maximum solution error and time order against the tighter reference. Peak time is resolved only on the output grid.

Scoped verification of an FHN/BVP-style reduced ODE. It excludes full HH ion channels, spatial axons, patient data and experimental electrophysiology reproduction.

## MCMC, temperature control and biological models — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-models/#fitzhugh-nagumo-references
Coverage: reading

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
R. FitzHugh (1961). Impulses and Physiological States in Theoretical Models of Nerve Membrane · DOI: 10.1016/S0006-3495(61)86902-6
Review scope / review_level: official-abstract-and-metadata
Original-paper abstract and bibliography in PubMed checked. Supports the two-variable excitable/refractory reduction; no full HH or measured membrane-voltage reproduction is claimed.
J. Nagumo, S. Arimoto and S. Yoshizawa (1962). An Active Pulse Transmission Line Simulating Nerve Axon · DOI: 10.1109/JRPROC.1962.288235
Review scope / review_level: publisher-abstract-and-metadata
IEEE publisher abstract, volume, pages and DOI checked. Historical source for reduced excitation and its circuit analogue; no spatial transmission-line or hardware-experiment reproduction is claimed.
The SciPy community (2024). SciPy1.14.1 solve_ivp reference
Review scope / review_level: official-api-documentation
Official DOP853, dense output, tolerance and success specifications checked. Implementation documentation for the separate numerical reference.

## Nonuniform ALE transport and2D rotating shallow-water waves — Nonuniform ALE transport and2D rotating shallow-water waves [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-moving-waves/
Coverage: reading

Time-advance conservative ALE transport on genuinely nonuniform moving cells with GCL, and2D linear rotating C-grid shallow-water waves. A prescribed-ALE Saltzman-type piston and limited sphere transport/axisymmetric balance are separate additions; general global Williamson dynamics remain unverified.

## Nonuniform ALE transport and2D rotating shallow-water waves — Download and execute the supplement [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-moving-waves/#run-all
Coverage: reading

Run inside atlas-moving-waves-2026-11-23 from the ZIP. This command executes all 2 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output
Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

## Nonuniform ALE transport and2D rotating shallow-water waves — ALE scalar transport on genuinely nonuniform moving cells [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-moving-waves/
Coverage: reading

Advance cell integrals and face positions with identical Heun stages, transporting a nonuniform analytic wave beyond a uniform GCL check.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
ALE uniform-state / geometric-conservation model
Upwind finite differences
Heun / SSPRK(2,2)
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Upwind relative flux(a-w)q advances actual masses with identical predictor/corrector face geometry; record stage volumes and Courant numbers.
ALE scalar conservation on moving cells
Periodic unit interval, speed.7,q0=1+.2sin(2pi x), grid speed .2sin(2pi xi)cos(2pi t),N40/80/160,T1. Separate N40,T.25 time series32/64/128steps.
Problem figure
A saved validation figure for this execution example. Its conditions and acceptance scope are documented by this page’s checks.
ALE scalar transport on genuinely nonuniform moving cells
This problem’s code and validation status
Exact / reference solutions
References and checks for this execution

## Noh:2D Cartesian flow and grid orientation error — Noh problem: an actual 2D Cartesian Euler calculation [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-noh-cartesian/
Coverage: reading

Reference and validation scope
Inputs/source/acceptance hashes are saved before execution. All 19 unit tests and 49 gates on three grids passed at the first attempt. Analytic density is integrated over cells by splitting shock-circle cuts and 64-point Gauss quadrature with x=rs sin(theta), checked against 128 points and analytic total mass; these are quadrature references, not closed-form exact cell means. At 128², full-square density L1=.09981, origin-inclusive core L1=.12231; shock errors are.968 axis cells and1.469 diagonal cells. Maximum relative discrete-budget residual is about 4.6e-15. D4 conserved parity and continuous rotational symmetry are measured separately.
Same-problem reference · Analytic reference
Noh cold-inflow shock: planar, cylindrical and spherical symmetry
Analytic reference for the same Noh problem.1D uses exact conserved-volume means;2D uses density means from shock-split Cartesian cell quadrature. Distinguish points/cell means and p(mean U)/mean p.

## Noh:2D Cartesian flow and grid orientation error — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-noh-cartesian/#noh-cartesian-2d-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Nondimensional [-.5,.5]², gamma=5/3, rho0=1, inward speed 1, p0=0, T=.6, shock radius.2. Initial conserved states are cell-center cold samples, not exact initial momentum means. All four edges prescribe supersonic inflow rho=1+t/r and u=(-x/r,-y/r). No symmetry boundary, radial projection or geometric source.

## Noh:2D Cartesian flow and grid orientation error — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-noh-cartesian/#noh-cartesian-2d-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Unsplit shared-face x/y piecewise-constant Rusanov fluxes and SSPRK2/Heun. CFL .35 uses (max a_x+max a_y)/dx. Cold physical outer fluxes are spatially integrated analytically and their affine time dependence is integrated at both Heun stages. No cell repair, pressure floor/seed or hidden timestep retry; invalid stages retain raw arrays and fail.
\partial_t U+\partial_xF(U)+\partial_yG(U)=0,\quad U=(\rho,\rho u,\rho v,E)^Tr_s=t/3,\quad(\rho,p,u_r)_2=(16,16/3,0),\quad(\rho,p,u_r)_1=(1+t/r,0,-1)\bar\rho_i=\frac{1}{\Delta x\Delta y}\int_{C_i}\rho_{\rm exact}(\sqrt{x^2+y^2},t)\,dx\,dyM(t)=4R^2+8Rt\operatorname{asinh}(1)+\pi t^2,\qquad E_{\rm tot}=M/2,\quad R=0.5\Delta t=\frac{0.35}{\max a_x/\Delta x+\max a_y/\Delta y}

At 128², full-square density L1=.09981, origin-inclusive core L1=.12231; shock errors are.968 axis cells and1.469 diagonal cells. Maximum relative discrete-budget residual is about 4.6e-15. ## Noh:2D Cartesian flow and grid orientation error — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-noh-cartesian/#noh-cartesian-2d-limits
Coverage: reading

A first-order-space lightweight example retains origin heating and shock errors. Finest maximum center specific internal energy is still about 14% high. Axis/diagonal shock-radius difference is about .501dx and is not monotone over these grids. Roundoff-level D4 parity does not establish exact circular symmetry. General perturbation stability, displaced origins, rotated meshes, 3D Cartesian flow and high-order accuracy are unverified. Earlier planar/cylindrical/spherical 1D editions and gates remain unchanged.

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
W. F. Noh (1987). Errors for calculations of strong shocks using an artificial viscosity and an artificial heat flux · DOI: 10.1016/0021-9991(87)90074-X
Review scope / review_level: publisher-metadata-and-abstract
Publisher metadata and abstract checked; full original text was not accessed (403). Cited for the problem and heating-error analysis, not as the source of this particular finite-volume discretization.
J. Thrussell and J. M. Ferguson (2023). ExactPack: A python library of exact analytic solutions · DOI: 10.1016/j.softx.2023.101560
Review scope / review_level: official-record-and-unmodified-pinned-code-execution
Selected pinned official Noh evaluator code checked. Reuse previously independently executed d=2 point values away from the jump; no new ExactPack execution or independent 2D PDE-engine comparison.

## Noh shocks: exact reference, origin heating and refinement — Noh shocks: zero-pressure planar, cylindrical and spherical flow [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-noh/
Coverage: reading

Rusanov flux with SSPRK2 (Heun). Planar/cylindrical runs retain piecewise-constant reconstruction. Spherical runs reconstruct conserved variables linearly around volume centroids with minmod slopes based on centroid distances in interior cells and zero slopes in the two boundary cells. A single theta per cell scales all conserved slopes at both faces to check face density/internal energy. Cell means are never corrected and no pressure seed/floor is used. Wave speeds, Rusanov flux and numerical stress P*=F_mom-((u_L+u_R)/2)F_mass use the same face states. The geometric CFL V/(A_La_L+A_Ra_R) uses the prescribed .35. Spherical source quadrature exactly integrates the face-linear numerical stress against 2r dr; planar/cylindrical runs keep the old arithmetic rule. Reconstructed reflection faces use even/odd parity, with physical cold inflow at the outer face. Every RK stage is checked and invalid states cause a retained failure.
Compressible Euler equations
The scoped planar, cylindrical-radial and spherical-radial forms of ideal-gas Euler. This example defines the geometric source, outer inflow and exactly zero initial pressure in its formulas and fixed input.
Problem figure
A saved validation figure for this execution example. Its conditions and acceptance scope are documented by this page’s checks.
Noh problem: cold converging flow and outward shock

## Noh shocks: exact reference, origin heating and refinement — Noh shocks: zero-pressure planar, cylindrical and spherical flow [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-noh/
Coverage: reading

Retain the planar/cylindrical acceptance file and all 59 original decisions, and save spherical criteria, inputs and source hashes before the first spherical PDE run. The initial cylindrical failure retains its source, all eight diagnostic logs and failed summary; the face-stress revision was tested against the same gates. Analytic conserved means split shock-crossing integrals and distinguish p(mean U) from mean p. The pinned independent LANL ExactPack analytic comparison includes d=1/2/3. New spherical PDE refinements separately measure full-domain r^2-weighted L1/L2/Linf, density L1 in r<=.70rs including the origin, and center/shock/plateau diagnostics. Discrete stage-weighted inflow budgets are distinct from continuous analytic totals; SSPRK2 boundary quadrature is checked through M_h-M_exact=sum(dt^3)/6 and E_h-E_exact=sum(dt^3)/12. The first spherical run retained arithmetic source quadrature and failed two of 105 gates (finest shock-position error 3.923 cells, plateau-density error 11.03%); all results are retained. A second attempt changed only spherical stress quadrature, but still failed the same two gates (3.919 cells and 11.018% density error). A third attempt retains that quadrature and adds MUSCL/minmod reconstruction only for spherical runs, against the same 105 criteria. The third attempt completed 28 tests and all 12 grid runs, passing all 105 gates. At spheric

## Noh shocks: exact reference, origin heating and refinement — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-noh/#noh-shock-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Nondimensional r in [0,1], gamma=5/3, rho0=1, u0=-1, p0=0, T=.6. PDE runs use planar d=1, cylindrical-radial d=2 and spherical-radial d=3, with shock radius .2. Outer density is (1+t)^(d-1), the origin reflects, and the measure is r^(d-1)dr. The same angular factor is omitted throughout; spherical analytic totals are M=512/375 and E=256/375. Its figure is a central section of a 1D radial solution, not a Cartesian 2D/3D calculation or a test of angular symmetry breaking.

## Noh shocks: exact reference, origin heating and refinement — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-noh/#noh-shock-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Rusanov flux with SSPRK2 (Heun). Planar/cylindrical runs retain piecewise-constant reconstruction. Spherical runs reconstruct conserved variables linearly around volume centroids with minmod slopes based on centroid distances in interior cells and zero slopes in the two boundary cells. A single theta per cell scales all conserved slopes at both faces to check face density/internal energy. Cell means are never corrected and no pressure seed/floor is used. Wave speeds, Rusanov flux and numerical stress P*=F_mom-((u_L+u_R)/2)F_mass use the same face states. The geometric CFL V/(A_La_L+A_Ra_R) uses the prescribed .35. Spherical source quadrature exactly integrates the face-linear numerical stress against 2r dr; planar/cylindrical runs keep the old arithmetic rule. Reconstructed reflection faces use even/odd parity, with physical cold inflow at the outer face. Every RK stage is checked and invalid states cause a retained failure.

## Noh shocks: exact reference, origin heating and refinement — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-noh/#noh-shock-algorithm

\partial_tU+r^{1-d}\partial_r(r^{d-1}F(U))=(0,(d-1)p/r,0)^T,\quad U=(\rho,\rho u,E)^TC=(\gamma+1)/(\gamma-1),\quad r_s=|u_0|(\gamma-1)t/2,\quad \rho_2=\rho_0C^d,\quad p_2=(\gamma-1)\rho_2u_0^2/2\rho_1(r,t)=\rho_0(1+|u_0|t/r)^{d-1},\quad u_1=u_0,\quad p_1=0V_i=(r_{i+1/2}^d-r_{i-1/2}^d)/d,\quad P_f^*=\widehat F_{m,f}-\bar u_f\widehat F_{\rho,f},\quad \text{arithmetic-face option: }S_{m,i}V_i=\tfrac12(P_{i-1/2}^*+P_{i+1/2}^*)(A_{i+1/2}-A_{i-1/2})\mathcal E_1=\frac{\sum_iV_i|\bar\rho_i-\bar\rho_i^{\rm exact}|}{\sum_iV_i\bar\rho_i^{\rm exact}},\quad M(t)=\rho_0(R+|u_0|t)^d/d,\quad E_{\rm tot}(t)=u_0^2M(t)/2d=3,\ \rho_0=|u_0|=1:\quad M_h-M_{\rm exact}=\frac16\sum_n\Delta t_n^3,\qquad E_h-E_{\rm exact}=\frac1{12}\sum_n\Delta t_n^3\mathcal E_{\rm core}=\frac{\sum_{r_{i+1/2}\le0.70r_s}V_i|\bar\rho_i-\bar\rho_i^{\rm exact}|}{\sum_{r_{i+1/2}\le0.70r_s}V_i\bar\rho_i^{\rm exact}},\qquad V_i=\frac{r_{i+1/2}^3-r_{i-1/2}^3}{3}d=3:\quad \int_a^b2rP^*(r)\,dr=\frac{b-a}{3}\big[(b+2a)P_L^*+(2b+a)P_R^*\big]\bar r_i=\frac{d}{d+1}\frac{r_{i+1/2}^{d+1}-r_{i-1/2}^{d+1}}{r_{i+1/2}^{d}-r_{i-1/2}^{d}},\qquad U_i(r)=\bar U_i+\theta_i\sigma_i(r-\bar r_i)\sigma_i=\operatorname{minmod}\left(\frac{\bar U_i-\bar U_{i-1}}{\bar r_i-\bar r_{i-1}},\frac{\bar U_{i+1}-\bar U_i}{\bar r_{i+1}-\bar r_i}\right),\quad 0\le\theta_i\le1\quad \text{interior cells; boundary slopes }\sigma_0=\sigma_{N-1}=0

## Noh shocks: exact reference, origin heating and refinement — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-noh/#noh-shock-limits
Coverage: reading

An educational calculation: first-order space in planar/cylindrical flow and MUSCL-type limited linear reconstruction in spherical flow. Origin heating and finite-grid plateau errors remain; the center is never removed from whole-domain error. Because r^2 weighting can make central defects appear small, an origin-inclusive fixed-core norm and enlarged view are also shown. Vanishing Linf/center maximum error, high order for the complete method on smooth spherical problems, general stage positivity with the geometric source, Cartesian multidimensional flow and independent arbitrary-gamma validation are not established. Cylindrical Linf was not monotone in the old series; spherical L2/Linf and heating are retained as diagnostics. Roundoff-scale discrete mass/energy balance coexists with O(dt^2) spherical boundary-time-quadrature error against analytic totals. Radial momentum has a geometric source and is not a conserved Cartesian momentum component. ExactPack independently implements the analytic evaluator, not another numerical PDE engine.

## Noh shocks: exact reference, origin heating and refinement — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-noh/#noh-shock-references
Coverage: reading

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
W. F. Noh (1987). Errors for calculations of strong shocks using an artificial viscosity and an artificial heat flux · DOI: 10.1016/0021-9991(87)90074-X
Review scope / review_level: publisher-metadata-and-abstract
Publisher metadata and abstract checked; full original text was not accessed (403). Cited for the problem and heating-error analysis, not as the source of this particular finite-volume discretization.
J. Thrussell and J. M. Ferguson (2023). ExactPack: A python library of exact analytic solutions · DOI: 10.1016/j.softx.2023.101560
Review scope / review_level: official-record-and-unmodified-pinned-code-execution
Checked the LANL software record and separately executed unmodified Noh code at commit 9bacc477eb791e959c9621e771fc7a725db755fa. Cross-checks use only gamma=5/3 and rho0=|u0|=1: points and shock-split Gauss integration of conservative means. Retain that d=3 analytic-comparison receipt; this edition separately executes its spherical PDE series.
van Leer, Bram (1979). Towards the ultimate conservative difference scheme. V. A second-order sequel to Godunov's method · DOI: 10.1016/0021-9991(79)90145-1

Existing Atlas bibliography record. Background for limited linear reconstruction and limiters, not a claim to reproduce the full original algorithm or a general positivity theorem for geometric-source zero-pressure Euler.
Mignone, Andrea (2014). High-order conservative reconstruction schemes for finite volume methods in cylindrical and spherical coordinates · DOI: 10.1016/j.jcp.2014.04.001

Selected original arXiv sections 2.2, 3.1 and 4.2 checked for volume centroids, conservative linear reconstruction and source integration. The restricted minmod/Rusanov/Heun and numerical-stress source are Atlas choices, distinct from reproducing the full paper scheme.

## Stiff ODEs, RK45 and boundary splitting — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-ode-adaptivity/#robertson-stiff-kinetics-algorithm
Coverage: reading

BDF2 starts with backward Euler on the same grid. SDIRK2 stages use a weighted maximum residual and reuse Jacobian factors only within one stage. Adaptive steps use an RMS step-doubling estimate and accept the two-half-step result.
\dot y_1=-0.04y_1+10^4y_2y_3,\quad\dot y_2=-\dot y_1-3\!\times\!10^7y_2^2,\quad\dot y_3=3\!\times\!10^7y_2^2\|r\|_{w,\infty}=\max_i|r_i|/w_i,\quad e_{\rm dbl}=(y_{h/2,h/2}-y_h)/3

## Stiff ODEs, RK45 and boundary splitting — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-ode-adaptivity/#rk45-dense-events-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Use actual Dormand–Prince 5(4) stages, a quartic continuous extension, an accepted-state derivative cache and bracket bisection on retained interpolants. A rejected endpoint never replaces the accepted starting derivative.
y(t)=e^{-0.2t}(\cos 3t,\sin 3t)^T,\quad t_*=\pi/6,\pi/2y(t_n+\theta h)=y_n+hQ(\theta,\theta^2,\theta^3,\theta^4)^T

Centered spatial difference

Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
For w = u - 1, use the unmodified split (Lw, w + 1) or the corrected split (Lw + 1, w). Compose actual Dirichlet DST-I flows and retain the reaction boundary mismatch.
Linear reaction-diffusion with inhomogeneous boundaries
Solve u_t = u_xx + u on [0, 1] with both boundary values equal to 1, an analytic steady state plus a 0.1 sine perturbation, and T = 0.1. Use 31, 63 and 127 interior nodes with 8, 16, 32 and 64 steps, plus four Lie controls: 28 runs.

First qualify an independent sparse affine exponential action against separately written sine sums. Then separate temporal error against the same finite-difference system, spatial error against the analytic continuum field, and observed order in the fixed regime.

Coverage: reading

Run inside atlas-particle-transport-2026-11-22 from the ZIP. This command executes all 6 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output
Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

## Particles and transport: independent references, conservation and statistical error — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particle-transport/#ewald-convergence-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Coulomb constant one; unit cubic 3D periodic neutral cell with tin-foil boundary. The asymmetric configuration matches the earlier example; reference zero-mode and self conventions match the model.

## Particles and transport: independent references, conservation and statistical error — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particle-transport/#ewald-convergence-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Independently integrate the Gaussian representation of 1/r and products of one-dimensional theta sums. Use a Poisson transform and analytic neutrality cancellation at small integration arguments, and self-subtracted image sums at large arguments. Integrate analytic theta derivatives for forces.
E=\frac{1}{\sqrt\pi}\int_0^\infty\left[\sum_{ij}q_iq_j\Theta(\mathbf r_i-\mathbf r_j,u)-\sum_iq_i^2\right]du\mathbf F_i=-\nabla_iE

## Particles and transport: independent references, conservation and statistical error — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particle-transport/#ewald-convergence-limits
Coverage: reading

One fixed neutral cubic cell. Upper-limit sensitivity is not a rigorous tail bound for arbitrary configurations. The theta reference is an independently formulated original implementation, not an external package or published numerical table. Charged/triclinic/slab cells, stress and long MD are outside scope.

Free-space phi=−sum(q log r), excluding self terms. The unit square bounds the tree and is not a wall or periodic boundary; this is separate from a 3D Coulomb kernel.

## Particles and transport: independent references, conservation and statistical error — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particle-transport/#fmm-convergence-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Retain P2M/M2M/M2L/L2L and near P2P; compare orders 2/4/8/12 and depths two/three. References include independent Cartesian direct sums, a closed-form charge pair and regular-polygon radial/far-field identities.
\phi_i=-\sum_{j\ne i}q_j\log|z_i-z_j|,\qquad\mathbf F_i=q_i\mathbf E_i\epsilon_E=\max_i\|\mathbf E_i^{\rm FMM}-\mathbf E_i^{\rm direct}\|_{\infty}

## Particles and transport: independent references, conservation and statistical error — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particle-transport/#pic-conservation-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Length 2pi, stationary unit-density ions, electron q/m=−1, plasma frequency one, sinusoidal displacement 0.001 and final time 1.6. Mesh runs retain 2048 particles; time runs retain a 32-cell mesh and 256 particles. The particle weight is w=2pi/N and n is the grid count.

## Particles and transport: independent references, conservation and statistical error — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particle-transport/#pic-conservation-algorithm
Coverage: reading

CIC deposition/matched gathering, spectral Poisson and velocity Verlet. The independent time algorithm DOP853 integrates the same particle-grid RHS; compare its own maximum-step refinements.
\mathbb E[|\widehat\rho_1/n|^2]=\frac{2+\cos(2\pi/n)}{3N}H_h=\frac{w}{2}\sum_iv_i^2+\frac{\Delta x}{2}\sum_jE_j^2

## Particles and transport: independent references, conservation and statistical error — DSMC collision component: finite-N equilibrium, invariants and statistical error [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particle-transport/
Coverage: reading

Check maximum momentum/energy errors over all rounds against deterministic tolerances. Use independent-seed standard errors for six-round anisotropy, four energy-CDF points and fourth moments against the finite-N beta reference. Separate decreasing CDF sampling error with N from finite-N Maxwell bias.
No corresponding reference-library card is registered. The execution-specific validation material above documents its reference values and acceptance checks.
Input and validation protocol history · Initial input

## Particles and transport: independent references, conservation and statistical error — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particle-transport/#dsmc-statistics-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Homogeneous equal-mass isotropic Maxwell collisions; N=16/64/256, 64 independent seeds, zero momentum and sum|v|²=3N. Start with two beams and run 24 collision rounds; rounds are not calibrated physical time.

## Particles and transport: independent references, conservation and statistical error — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particle-transport/#dsmc-statistics-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Uniform random complete matchings and isotropic pair scattering preserve pair momentum/energy. An independent sampler projects Gaussian vectors into the zero-center-of-mass subspace and fixes their radius.
\frac{e_i}{3(N-1)/2}\sim\mathrm{Beta}\!\left(\frac32,\frac{3(N-2)}2\right)\mathbb E[v_x^4]=\frac{9(N-1)}{3N-1},\qquad\mathbb E[D_r]=3\left[\frac{N-2}{2(N-1)}\right]^re_i=|\mathbf v_i|^2/2,\qquad D_r=\langle v_x^2-(v_y^2+v_z^2)/2\rangle_r

## Particles and transport: independent references, conservation and statistical error — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particle-transport/#dsmc-statistics-validation
Coverage: reading

Check maximum momentum/energy errors over all rounds against deterministic tolerances. Use independent-seed standard errors for six-round anisotropy, four energy-CDF points and fourth moments against the finite-N beta reference. Separate decreasing CDF sampling error with N from finite-N Maxwell bias.

## Particles and transport: independent references, conservation and statistical error — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particle-transport/#dsmc-statistics-limits
Coverage: reading

Statistical diagnostics cover fixed 64-seed ensembles, not every seed. Conservation correlates particles within a seed; do not use IID KS p-values. No spatial streaming, collision cells, speed-dependent hard-sphere selection or transport coefficients.

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particle-transport/#dsmc-statistics-references
Coverage: reading

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
G. A. Bird (1963). Approach to Translational Equilibrium in a Rigid Sphere Gas · DOI: 10.1063/1.1710976
Review scope / review_level: metadata-only
Official Sandia DSMC commemorative document and DOI metadata checked; publisher text unavailable and the original hard-sphere model is not claimed as reproduced.
E. Scalas, A. T. Gabriel, E. Martin and G. Germano (2015). Velocity and energy distributions in microcanonical ensembles of hard spheres · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevE.92.022140
Review scope / review_level: primary-abstract-and-selected-theory; separate center-of-mass sphere derivation
Initial design reviewed the abstract; subsequent additional review consulted selected finite-system theory. Explicitly derive the zero-momentum sphere marginal here; no original molecular-dynamics data are reused.
Official reference-implementation documentation: scipy.special.betainc.html

## Particles and transport: independent references, conservation and statistical error — Radiation transport: space/angle convergence and photon statistics [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particle-transport/
Coverage: reading

Refine 16–256 cells and 4–64 ordinates separately; compare QUADPACK integration with E3. For 64 seeds and 1024/4096/16384 photons, record mean error, RMSE, binomial standard deviation and observed 95% Clopper–Pearson coverage. Check photon exit-plus-absorption counts, positivity and discrete flux balance.
No corresponding reference-library card is registered. The execution-specific validation material above documents its reference values and acceptance checks.
Input and validation protocol history · Initial input

## Particles and transport: independent references, conservation and statistical error — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particle-transport/#radiation-convergence-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Steady uniform slab, optical depths .1/.7/3, unit incoming positive-hemisphere intensity, no reverse inflow/scattering/emission. Incoming photon directions for a flux estimator have density 2mu.

## Particles and transport: independent references, conservation and statistical error — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particle-transport/#radiation-convergence-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Use upstream finite volumes and Gauss-Legendre ordinates; exact exponential propagation removes spatial error in the angle series. Monte Carlo independently tracks survival/absorption using mu=sqrt(U) and exponential optical paths.
F_{\rm out}=2\pi E_3(\tau)=\pi p,\qquad\mu=\sqrt U\sigma_{\widehat F}=\pi\sqrt{p(1-p)/N_\gamma}

## Particles and transport: independent references, conservation and statistical error — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particle-transport/#radiation-convergence-validation
Coverage: reading

Refine 16–256 cells and 4–64 ordinates separately; compare QUADPACK integration with E3. For 64 seeds and 1024/4096/16384 photons, record mean error, RMSE, binomial standard deviation and observed 95% Clopper–Pearson coverage. Check photon exit-plus-absorption counts, positivity and discrete flux balance.

## Particles and transport: independent references, conservation and statistical error — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particle-transport/#radiation-convergence-limits
Coverage: reading

Coverage is observed over finite fixed seeds; neither exactly 95% empirical coverage nor all-seed success is guaranteed. Keep deterministic quadrature error separate from statistical error. Multiple scattering, frequency dependence, thermal emission and radiation hydrodynamics are unvalidated.
