## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#ewald-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Combine an erfc-screened image sum, Gaussian-damped reciprocal structure factors and the self correction. Differentiate each term and check all 24 force components against central energy differences.
E=\frac12\sum_{ij\mathbf n}^{\prime}q_iq_j\frac{\operatorname{erfc}(\alpha r_{ij\mathbf n})}{r_{ij\mathbf n}}+\frac{2\pi}{V}\sum_{\mathbf k\ne0}\frac{e^{-k^2/(4\alpha^2)}}{k^2}|S(\mathbf k)|^2-\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt\pi}\sum_iq_i^2M_{\rm NaCl}=\frac2{\sqrt\pi}\int_0^\infty[1-\vartheta_4(0,e^{-u^2})^3]du

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#fmm-assumptions

Particles lie in a unit-square bounding box, not a physical wall boundary. The kernel is phi=−sum(q log r), with field −grad(phi); self terms are excluded and no periodic images are used.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#fmm-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Implement leaf P2M, upward M2M, interaction-list M2L, downward L2L, local-polynomial evaluation and near-field P2P. Record translation and near-pair counts; this is not a Barnes–Hut traversal relabeled as FMM.
M_k(c)=\sum_jq_j(z_j-c)^kf(z)=M_0\log(z-c)-\sum_{k=1}^p\frac{M_k}{k(z-c)^k},\qquad\phi=-\Re f

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#pic-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Dimensionless length 2pi, electron charge/mass −1, stationary ion density one and plasma frequency one. A quiet start receives a small sinusoidal displacement of amplitude 0.001.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#pic-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Combine CIC deposition and matching field gathering, a mean-zero spectral Poisson solve and velocity Verlet. Set the field Nyquist mode to zero for a real skew-adjoint spectral derivative.
\dot x_i=v_i,\quad\dot v_i=-E_h(x_i),\quad-\phi_{xx}=\rho,\quad E=-\phi_xA(t)/A(0)\simeq\cos(\omega_pt),\qquad\omega_p=1

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#pic-validation
Coverage: reading

Separate a 32/64/128-grid sweep from timestep refinement on a 512 grid. Compare displacement amplitude with continuum linear cos(t), and check charge compatibility, potential-Poisson residual and single-particle self force.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#pic-limits
Coverage: reading

Finite amplitude and finite particles leave an error floor. Nonlinear instabilities, Landau damping, collisions, electromagnetic/relativistic PIC and open particle boundaries are unvalidated.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Conservation and Maxwell relaxation in a homogeneous DSMC collision component [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/
Coverage: reading

Use 512/2048/8192 particles and sixteen seeds to check momentum/energy, Maxwell second/fourth moments and the Gamma(3/2,1) energy CDF. Independently check the expected per-round anisotropy factor (N−2)/(2(N−1)). The finite-N component fourth moment is 3−6/(3N−1); distinguish that finite-particle offset from the across-seed sampling uncertainty.
No corresponding reference-library card is registered. The execution-specific validation material above documents its reference values and acceptance checks.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#dsmc-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Homogeneous, equal masses, isotropic scattering and constant collision rate. Each round randomly matches every particle once. Two initial beams at ±sqrt(3) give target temperature one. Each seed has zero total momentum and fixed total energy: its finite-N equilibrium is microcanonical, while Maxwell/Gamma are large-N references.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#dsmc-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Preserve pair center-of-mass velocity and relative speed, then choose the new relative direction uniformly on the sphere. Rounds count collision operations and are not calibrated physical time. For D=<vx²−(vy²+vz²)/2>, averaging a random partner multiplies the center-of-mass anisotropy by (N−2)/(2(N−1)); isotropic postcollision relative directions contribute zero expected anisotropy.
\mathbf v_{1,2}^{\prime}=\mathbf V\pm\frac{|\mathbf g|}{2}\mathbf n,\qquad|\mathbf n|=1\mathbb E[D_{r+1}]=\frac{N-2}{2(N-1)}\mathbb E[D_r]

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#dsmc-validation
Coverage: reading

Use 512/2048/8192 particles and sixteen seeds to check momentum/energy, Maxwell second/fourth moments and the Gamma(3/2,1) energy CDF. Independently check the expected per-round anisotropy factor (N−2)/(2(N−1)). The finite-N component fourth moment is 3−6/(3N−1); distinguish that finite-particle offset from the across-seed sampling uncertainty.

## Particles, electrostatics, kinetic and radiative transport — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-particles/#dsmc-limits
Coverage: reading

This is an educational DSMC collision component. No spatial streaming, collision cells, speed-dependent hard-sphere selection, measured transport coefficients/flow fields or every-seed guarantee. Bird’s original hard-sphere conditions are not reproduced.

## Small quantum models and saved-reference cards — Download and execute the supplement [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-quantum-small/#run-all
Coverage: reading

Run inside atlas-quantum-small-2026-11-25 from the ZIP. This command executes all 7 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output
Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

## Small quantum models and saved-reference cards — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-quantum-small/#two-state-bo-cp-ou-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Use analytic BO forces and the declared CP-type action with Verlet/BAOAB; record nuclear heat and fictitious electronic kinetic energy separately.
H(Q)=\frac{kQ^2}{2}I+\begin{pmatrix}-\Delta&gQ\\gQ&\Delta\end{pmatrix},\quad\psi=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)^TE(Q,\theta)=\frac{kQ^2}{2}-\Delta\cos(2\theta)+gQ\sin(2\theta),\quad E_-(Q)=\frac{kQ^2}{2}-\sqrt{\Delta^2+g^2Q^2}M\ddot Q=-kQ-g\sin(2\theta),\quad\mu\ddot\theta=-2\Delta\sin(2\theta)-2gQ\cos(2\theta)V^+=aV^-+\sqrt{(T/M)(1-a^2)}\,\xi,\quad a=e^{-\gamma h},\quad Q_{\rm bath}=\sum\Delta K_{\rm nuclear}

## Small quantum models and saved-reference cards — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-quantum-small/#quantum-box-ho-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Finite Dirichlet boxes and central differences; whole-line HO formulas do not isolate finite-wall error. Node counts diagnostic until forward sign qualification. Atomic model units hbar=m=1 and HO omega=1. The box[0,1] and finite HO[-L,L] domains both use homogeneous Dirichlet conditions.

## Small quantum models and saved-reference cards — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-quantum-small/#quantum-box-ho-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Use centered differences and eight full NumPy eigensolves, saving824 native pairs before selecting24 low pairs.
H_h=-\frac12D_{xx}+V,\quad V_{\rm box}=0,\quad V_{\rm HO}=x^2/2E_j^{\rm box}=\frac{(j\pi)^2}{2},\quad u_j=\sqrt2\sin(j\pi x),\quad\lambda_{h,j}=2h^{-2}\sin^2\left(\frac{j\pi}{2M}\right),\ h=1/ME_n^{\rm HO}=n+\frac12,\quad u_n(x)=\frac{H_n(x)e^{-x^2/2}}{\pi^{1/4}\sqrt{2^nn!}},\quad u_h=v_h/\sqrt h

## 2D shadows,beams and M1 closure — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-radiation-geometry/#shadow-absorber2d-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Conservative upwind angular finite volumes or M1 Rusanov fluxes with SSPRK2; exponential absorption with a separate deposited-energy ledger. Six axis directions have weight1/6; a unit beam has nodal intensity6. Retain Pzz and the full3D trace. No positive floor or cone projection. The revised general directional local-LF coefficient is the maximum of endpoint spectral radii,an independently derived cone-splitting bound,and normal reduced flux. Use the same face rule on all ghost boundaries and in the ledger. Explicit speed-only vacuum/allowed-roundoff extension1 is counted; no U/P projection or special beam branch. Preserve the original c1 transverse-diffusion failure.

## 2D shadows,beams and M1 closure — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-radiation-geometry/#opposing-beams2d-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Conservative upwind angular finite volumes or M1 Rusanov fluxes with SSPRK2; exponential absorption with a separate deposited-energy ledger. Six axis directions have weight1/6; a unit beam has nodal intensity6. Retain Pzz and the full3D trace. No positive floor or cone projection. The revised general directional local-LF coefficient is the maximum of endpoint spectral radii,an independently derived cone-splitting bound,and normal reduced flux. Use the same face rule on all ghost boundaries and in the ledger. Explicit speed-only vacuum/allowed-roundoff extension1 is counted; no U/P projection or special beam branch. Preserve the original c1 transverse-diffusion failure.
\partial_tE+\nabla\cdot\mathbf F=-\kappa_aE,\quad\partial_t\mathbf F+\nabla\cdot\mathbf P=-\kappa_a\mathbf F\mathbf P=E\left[\frac{1-\chi}{2}\mathbf I_3+\frac{3\chi-1}{2}\mathbf n\otimes\mathbf n\right]\chi=\frac{3+4f^2}{5+2\sqrt{4-3f^2}},\quad f=|\mathbf F|/E,\quad P_{xx}+P_{yy}+P_{zz}=E

## Non-equilibrium radiation: distinct diffusion and transport — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-radiation-matter/#su-olson-transport1997-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Full signed-angle upwind FV/SSPRK2 advancesIandV. WithI=2U,E=halfangularintegral,the weightedbudgetisepsilonE+V;nodiffusionsubstitution. Only the thick-limit control constructs the same upwind operator from actual real cos/sin responses and evolves one Fourier mode by an exact-time matrix exponential.
\epsilon I_\tau+\mu I_x+I=V+Q,\quad V_\tau=E-VE=\frac12\int_{-1}^1I\,d\mu,\quad I=2U,\quad\mathcal E=\epsilon E+VQ=\mathbf1_{|x|<1/2}\mathbf1_{0<\tau<10}\epsilon I_t+\mu I_x=\kappa(V-I),\quad V_t=\kappa(E-V),\quad x\in[0,2\pi)D_{\rm rad}=\frac1{3\kappa},\quad D_{\rm eff}=\frac1{3\kappa(\epsilon+1)},\quad t=\kappa sE_D=V_D=1+A_N e^{-s/[3(\epsilon+1)]}\cos x,\quad F_D=-\frac1{3\kappa}\partial_x E_D

## Isotropically scattering slabs and continuum-angle references — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-radiation-scattering/#isotropic-scattering-slab-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Conservative upwind FV with the full discrete angular source coupling solved by sweep-response elimination. Positive hemisphere Gauss weights normalize incoming fluxpi;absorption is independently accumulated from the volume source.
\mu\partial_xI+I=\omega J,\quad J=\frac12\int_{-1}^{1}I\,d\muJ(x)=\frac12E_2(x)+\frac\omega2\int_0^L E_1(|x-s|)J(s)\,dsR+T+A=1,\qquad A=4(1-\omega)\int_0^LJ\,dx

## SRHD collision and nonlinear SRMHD Alfven wave — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-relativistic/#srhd-collision-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Use the shared seven-component RMHD operator at B=0 with primitive MUSCL/minmod, causal HLL bounds±1 and SSPRK33. Safeguarded Newton recovers the physical Z=rho h W² root; check residual and full conserved-state roundtrip.
U=(D,S_x,S_y,S_z,E,B_y,B_z)^T,\quad D=\rho W,\quad W=(1-v^2)^{-1/2}h_b^2-h_a^2=(p_b-p_a)(h_b/\rho_b+h_a/\rho_a)v_0^2=\frac{(p_b-p_a)(e_b-e_a)}{(e_a+p_b)(e_b+p_a)},\quad e=\rho+\frac{p}{\Gamma-1}j^2=-\frac{p_b-p_a}{h_b/\rho_b-h_a/\rho_a},\quad V_s^2=\frac{j^2}{\rho_b^2+j^2}

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-relativistic/

Qualify nonlinear dispersion,independent tensor Gauss means and complex-step PDE residuals. Predeclare all-seven-component conservation,stage admissibility,intermediate errors,finest relative L1≤.04,phase≤.03,amplitude≤.04 and observed order≥1.5.
Same-problem reference · Analytic reference
SRMHD circular wave: finite-amplitude exact family and independent tensor integration
Use the original exact family with an independent lower-order operator; no ECHO-algorithm or error-table reproduction. Generic RMHD shocks,extreme magnetization/Lorentz factors,GR,resistive MHD and multidimensional divergence control are outside scope. Figures show actual1D x–t fields.

Flat spacetime,c=4pi=1,gamma4/3,rho=p=Bx=eta1, exact-family vx0. Rescale the original2pi period to a unit domain;64/128/256 cells,periodic,t=1/vA. Normal Bx is fixed in1D.

## SRHD collision and nonlinear SRMHD Alfven wave — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-relativistic/#srmhd-alfven-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Evolve all seven variables D,three momenta,total E and two transverse magnetic fields with the shared MUSCL/minmod–HLL–SSPRK33 operator. Magnetic dynamics are coupled; primitive recovery solves the full RMHD Z root.
B_y=\eta B_0\cos[2\pi(x-v_At)],\quad B_z=\eta B_0\sin[2\pi(x-v_At)]v_x=0,\quad (v_y,v_z)=-v_A(B_y,B_z)/B_0K=\rho h+B_0^2(1+\eta^2),\quad v_A^2=\frac{2B_0^2}{K+\sqrt{K^2-4\eta^2B_0^4}}\mathbf v=\frac{\mathbf S+(\mathbf S\cdot\mathbf B)\mathbf B/Z}{Z+B^2},\quad p=\frac{\Gamma-1}{\Gamma}(Z/W^2-\rho)E=Z-p+\frac12\left[B^2(1+v^2)-\frac{(\mathbf S\cdot\mathbf B)^2}{Z^2}\right]

Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used

Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
Piecewise-constant Rusanov fluxes on spherical shells with SSPRK2/Heun. The radial-momentum source p(A_right-A_left)/V is integrated at the same RK stages, with a stationary uniform-pressure balance test. CFL.4 uses the reciprocal maximum (|u|+c)/(V/(A_left+A_right)), comparing with the remaining interval before division. No pressure seed, floor, cell repair or hidden timestep retry; an invalid stage retains raw conserved values and history and fails.
Compressible Euler equations
The one-dimensional spherical-radial ideal-gas Euler system. This example defines origin reflection, geometric source, finite-radius energy deposition and outer boundary in its fixed input.

## Sedov–Taylor point blast: lightweight spherical-radial validation — Sedov–Taylor point blast: lightweight spherical-radial validation [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-sedov/
Coverage: reading

Original r1 passed22 tests and48 gates on Mac, but its public-ZIP Linux run failed when warnings-as-errors raised a cold-tail CFL overflow. Revision r2 uses the algebraically equivalent reciprocal maximum-rate evaluation while preserving the original inputs, reference and48 acceptance gates. A new r2-specific pre-execution hash contract precedes23 tests and all four calculations/48 gates passing with warnings as errors. Original sources, contract and actual Linux-failure evidence remain archived. The independent reference integrates the similarity ODE with DOP853, normalizes energy, uses a regular asymptote for xi<.001 and split shell quadrature at the shock. Orders16/32, core cutoff and ODE tolerance are checked separately. The unmodified pinned ExactPack evaluator was independently run at6001/12001 points and compared away from the center/jump with its preregistered5e-4 criterion. Beta=1.15166641793, Rs(.05)=.34746791233. Origin/shock-inclusive volume-weighted density L1 within r<=1.2Rs is.17257/.12785/.07458 and pressure L1 is.18148/.13939/.07615. Finest shock error is1.096 cells; maximum relative discrete-budget residual is about8.89e-16.
Same-problem reference · Semi-analytic reference
Sedov–Taylor point blast: energy-normalized spherical similarity solution

## Sedov–Taylor point blast: lightweight spherical-radial validation — Sedov–Taylor point blast: lightweight spherical-radial validation [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-sedov/
Coverage: reading

An energy-normalized spherical similarity reference. Numerical integration of similarity ODEs and shell quadrature make this semi-analytic, not closed-form exact cell means. Finite-radius deposition is distinct from the singular ideal point-blast initial data. At fixed finite deposition radius, comparison with the point-source similarity reference includes deposition-model discrepancy; its refinement slope is not a pure spatial order. Changing deposition radius on the same finest grid is a sensitivity diagnostic, not a complete separation of continuum deposition and PDE-discretization errors.

## Sedov–Taylor point blast: lightweight spherical-radial validation — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-sedov/#sedov-blast-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Nondimensional gamma=5/3, ambient density1, velocity0, pressure0, radius[0,1], deposited energy1, T=.05. Uniform thermal energy inside a sphere is assigned using exact cut-shell volumes. Deposition radius0.03 is shared by all three grids; a separate512-cell run uses0.015. The origin is reflecting and the outer boundary is outflow; actual boundary fluxes enter measured budgets.

## Sedov–Taylor point blast: lightweight spherical-radial validation — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-sedov/#sedov-blast-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Piecewise-constant Rusanov fluxes on spherical shells with SSPRK2/Heun. The radial-momentum source p(A_right-A_left)/V is integrated at the same RK stages, with a stationary uniform-pressure balance test. CFL.4 uses the reciprocal maximum (|u|+c)/(V/(A_left+A_right)), comparing with the remaining interval before division. No pressure seed, floor, cell repair or hidden timestep retry; an invalid stage retains raw conserved values and history and fails.
\partial_t U+\frac{1}{r^2}\partial_r(r^2F)=\left(0,2p/r,0\right)^T,\quad U=(\rho,\rho u,E)^TR_s(t)=\beta(E_0t^2/\rho_0)^{1/5},\quad\beta\simeq1.15166641793,\quad\dot R_s=2R_s/(5t)\rho=\rho_0G(\xi),\quad u=\dot R_sV(\xi),\quad p=\rho_0\dot R_s^2P(\xi),\quad\xi=r/R_sE_0=4\pi\int_0^\infty\left(\frac{p}{\gamma-1}+\frac{\rho u^2}{2}\right)r^2\,dr=1\bar U_i=\frac{3}{r_{i+1/2}^3-r_{i-1/2}^3}\int_{r_{i-1/2}}^{r_{i+1/2}}U(r)r^2\,dr

## Sedov–Taylor point blast: lightweight spherical-radial validation — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-sedov/#sedov-blast-validation
Coverage: reading

Original r1 passed22 tests and48 gates on Mac, but its public-ZIP Linux run failed when warnings-as-errors raised a cold-tail CFL overflow. Revision r2 uses the algebraically equivalent reciprocal maximum-rate evaluation while preserving the original inputs, reference and48 acceptance gates. A new r2-specific pre-execution hash contract precedes23 tests and all four calculations/48 gates passing with warnings as errors. Original sources, contract and actual Linux-failure evidence remain archived. The independent reference integrates the similarity ODE with DOP853, normalizes energy, uses a regular asymptote for xi<.001 and split shell quadrature at the shock. Orders16/32, core cutoff and ODE tolerance are checked separately. The unmodified pinned ExactPack evaluator was independently run at6001/12001 points and compared away from the center/jump with its preregistered5e-4 criterion. Beta=1.15166641793, Rs(.05)=.34746791233. Origin/shock-inclusive volume-weighted density L1 within r<=1.2Rs is.17257/.12785/.07458 and pressure L1 is.18148/.13939/.07615. Finest shock error is1.096 cells; maximum relative discrete-budget residual is about8.89e-16.

## Sedov–Taylor point blast: lightweight spherical-radial validation — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-sedov/#sedov-blast-limits
Coverage: reading

A finite deposition sphere and an ideal point blast have different initial data; reported errors combine deposition-model and discretization effects. The refinement slope is not a pure spatial order. Halving the source radius at the same512 cells changes density by about.000451 and pressure by.000619, but point-reference errors become slightly worse; no improvement or point-source-limit proof is claimed. Pressure compares numerical p(mean conserved U) with reference mean physical pressure, distinct from p(mean reference U). Center values and maximum errors remain reported. The finest density peak is about2.918 versus the exact jump4. The cold-tail local-CFL overflow that caused the r1 Linux failure is avoided in r2 by the equivalent maximum inverse-rate evaluation, without suppressing warnings or adding a physical floor. The regular tiny-core continuation is approximate, and ExactPack point probes exclude xi<.15. Cartesian2D/3D, general perturbations/asymmetry and high-order accuracy are unverified.

## Shallow water: topography, lakes and dry beds — SWASHES topographic flow: lakes and nonzero steady discharge [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-shallow-water/
Coverage: reading

Check two lake equilibria separately from nonzero subcritical flow, distinguishing lake preservation from moving-flow discretization error.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Godunov-type finite volumes
HLL
Forward Euler
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
Hydrostatic reconstruction, shared HLL flux and left/right pressure corrections discretize the bed source; forward Euler and face CFL .4. Lakes use reflecting walls. Moving subcritical boundaries impose upstream q and downstream h, extrapolating the other datum. No state floors, clipping or retries. Algebraically factor HLL updates into nonnegative water packets; advected momentum uses those same rounded masses, without a small-depth threshold or subsequent repair.
Shallow-water equations with bed source
1D, g=9.81, L=25m, compact parabolic bed z=.2-.05(x-10)^2 on8<x<12. Lakes at surface .5/.1m use200 cells. Moving flow q=4.42m2/s, downstream h=2m uses100/200/400 cells to2s. Initialize the steady branch, not the published rest-to-steady transient.

## Shallow water: topography, lakes and dry beds — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-shallow-water/#swashes-topography-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Hydrostatic reconstruction, shared HLL flux and left/right pressure corrections discretize the bed source; forward Euler and face CFL .4. Lakes use reflecting walls. Moving subcritical boundaries impose upstream q and downstream h, extrapolating the other datum. No state floors, clipping or retries. Algebraically factor HLL updates into nonnegative water packets; advected momentum uses those same rounded masses, without a small-depth threshold or subsequent repair.
\partial_t h+\partial_x q=0,\qquad \partial_tq+\partial_x(q^2/h+gh^2/2)=-gh\partial_xzz^*=\max(z_L,z_R),\quad h_K^*=\max(0,h_K+z_K-z^*),\quad q_K^*=h_K^*u_KF_K=F_{\mathrm{HLL}}(U_L^*,U_R^*)+(0,\tfrac12g(h_K^2-(h_K^*)^2))^Tq=4.42,\quad h+z+q^2/(2gh^2)=2+4.42^2/(8g),\quad h>(q^2/g)^{1/3}

Coverage: reading

Freeze31 unit checks and eight group runs. Record lake drift, every FE minimum depth, shared-flux/bed-impulse budgets, conservative-mean L1 errors and three-grid ratios. Qualify an independent Bernoulli bisection by energy and branch checks.

## Shallow water: topography, lakes and dry beds — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-shallow-water/#swashes-topography-limits
Coverage: reading

Exact lake balance concerns the represented cell bed. Moving steady states retain finite-time numerical error. Transcritical flows, jumps, friction, rain, infiltration, 2D flow and fully discrete entropy stability are outside scope.

The .001m mean-depth contour differs from the analytic support edge, which is reported separately. These fixed runs test wetting of initially dry cells. Retreating shorelines, re-drying cycles, real floods, friction and moving fronts over topography are outside scope. The initial100/200/400-cell [-5,5]m attempt passed28 tests and105/109 gates; three retained-dry-cell gates and the .3960m>.25m contour error failed. All original records remain archived; revision2 enlarges/refines the input without changing acceptance. Revision2 then stopped on a binary64 subnormal-tail dry-momentum artifact. ## Shallow water: topography, lakes and dry beds — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-shallow-water/#dry-bed-dam-break-algorithm
Coverage: reading

The FV solver supports h=q=0 directly; one-sided dry HLL speeds use u-c/u+2c and their reflection. Forward Euler at face CFL .4 records every minimum and shared-flux budget without raising cell depths. Algebraically factor HLL updates into nonnegative water packets; advected momentum uses those same rounded masses, without a small-depth threshold or subsequent repair.
c_L=\sqrt{gh_L},\quad x_A=x_0-c_Lt,\quad x_B=x_0+2c_Lth=(2c_L-(x-x_0)/t)^2/(9g),\quad u=\tfrac23((x-x_0)/t+c_L)\quad (x_A<x<x_B)\bar U_i^{\mathrm{ref}}=\Delta x^{-1}\int_{C_i}(h,hu)^Tdx,\quad x_{.001}=x_B-3t\sqrt{g(0.001)}

## Shallow water: topography, lakes and dry beds — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-shallow-water/#dry-bed-dam-break-limits
Coverage: reading

The .001m mean-depth contour differs from the analytic support edge, which is reported separately. These fixed runs test wetting of initially dry cells. Retreating shorelines, re-drying cycles, real floods, friction and moving fronts over topography are outside scope. The initial100/200/400-cell [-5,5]m attempt passed28 tests and105/109 gates; three retained-dry-cell gates and the .3960m>.25m contour error failed. All original records remain archived; revision2 enlarges/refines the input without changing acceptance. Revision2 then stopped on a binary64 subnormal-tail dry-momentum artifact. Revision3 factors the same HLL update into water packets and adds three regression/equivalence tests; the original28 remain unchanged. Revision3 passed108/109 gates but failed the .27415m>.25m contour criterion. Revision4 refines only Ritter grids to1600/3200/6400. Relative depth L1 is normalized by domain reference mass; absolute L1 is also retained because the domain changed between revisions1 and2.

Coverage: reading

Integrate all four states with SDIRK2 step doubling, using the same weighted L∞ residual for Newton convergence and Armijo backtracking. Evolve the reduced Michaelis–Menten equation separately with RK4 in θ, keeping integration error distinct from model-reduction error.
\begin{aligned}\dot S&=-10ES+C,&\dot C&=10ES-2C,\\\dot E&=-10ES+2C,&\dot P&=C.\end{aligned}E+C=E_0,\quad S+C+P=1,\quad K_m=\frac{k_{-1}+k_2}{k_1}=0.2\theta=E_0t,\quad \varepsilon=\frac{E_0}{K_m+S_0}\in\left\{\frac1{120},\frac1{600}\right\}\frac{dS_{\rm MM}}{d\theta}=-\frac{S_{\rm MM}}{0.2+S_{\rm MM}},\quad S_{\rm MM}+0.2\log S_{\rm MM}=1-\theta

\begin{aligned}\dot S&=-\beta SI,&\dot E&=\beta SI-\sigma E,\\\dot I&=\sigma E-\gamma I,&\dot R&=\gamma I.\end{aligned}\beta=0.6,\quad\sigma=0.3,\quad\gamma=0.2,\quad(S,E,I,R)(0)=(1-2\eta,\eta,\eta,0)S+E+I+R=1,\quad\eta\in\{10^{-4},5\times10^{-5}\}\begin{pmatrix}E_{\rm lin}(t)\\ I_{\rm lin}(t)\end{pmatrix}=\exp\!\left[t\begin{pmatrix}-0.3&0.6\\0.3&-0.2\end{pmatrix}\right]\begin{pmatrix}\eta\\\eta\end{pmatrix}

Advance a 32-point Schnakenberg reaction–diffusion problem to T=1 with matched inputs and subsolvers. Four step sizes check first-/second-order temporal convergence, reference sensitivity, reaction balance and failure on nonconvergence in a lightweight comparison.

Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
Lie–Trotter uses diffusion(h) then reaction(h); Strang uses diffusion(h/2), reaction(h), diffusion(h/2), always passing the updated state. Both apply the exact exponential of the centered-FD diffusion matrix by FFT and the same implicit-midpoint reaction/Newton tolerance 2e−13 with at most 12 residual evaluations. Reference and validation scope
The reference independently assembles the SAME FD semidiscretization with a real-space sparse matrix and separately written reaction RHS, then integrates it unsplit with Radau. Tighter Radau and separate DOP853 runs measure reference sensitivity relative to the finest Strang error. Norms are per-species mean L1, RMS L2 and maximum L∞, then the worse species; refinement uses the maximum across the four common positive observation times. ## Operator splitting: Lie–Trotter and Strang on the same reaction–diffusion problem — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-splitting/#reaction-diffusion-splitting-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Nondimensional 1D periodic [0,2pi), N=32, a=.1, b=.9, D=(.01,1). The initial fields u₀=1+.08cos2x+.01cos4x and v₀=.9−.03cos2x−.002cos4x match the earlier finite-amplitude example. This new run ends at T=1, uses 16/32/64/128 steps and common output times 0/.25/.5/.75/1. The fixed input is reflection-even and pi-periodic.

## Operator splitting: Lie–Trotter and Strang on the same reaction–diffusion problem — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-splitting/#reaction-diffusion-splitting-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Lie–Trotter uses diffusion(h) then reaction(h); Strang uses diffusion(h/2), reaction(h), diffusion(h/2), always passing the updated state. Both apply the exact exponential of the centered-FD diffusion matrix by FFT and the same implicit-midpoint reaction/Newton tolerance 2e−13 with at most 12 residual evaluations. The reaction flow is a second-order approximation, not exact. No clipping, adaptive steps or fallback; nonconvergence is failure.
u_t=0.01u_{xx}+0.1-u+u^2v,\qquad v_t=v_{xx}+0.9-u^2v\lambda_{h,k}=-\frac{4}{\Delta x^2}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\pi k}{N}\right),\quad L_h=\Psi_R^h\circ e^{hD L_{\rm FD}},\quad S_h=e^{hD L_{\rm FD}/2}\circ\Psi_R^h\circ e^{hD L_{\rm FD}/2}\Psi_R^h(y)=y+hR\!\left(\frac{y+\Psi_R^h(y)}2\right),\quad \langle u+v\rangle_{n+1}-\langle u+v\rangle_n=h(0.1+0.9-\langle u_{\rm mid}\rangle)E_2(h)=\max_{t\in\{.25,.5,.75,1\}}\max_{s\in\{u,v\}}\sqrt{\frac1N\sum_j(e_{s,j}(t))^2},\quad p_{\rm obs}=\log_2\frac{E_2(h)}{E_2(h/2)}

## Operator splitting: Lie–Trotter and Strang on the same reaction–diffusion problem — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-splitting/#reaction-diffusion-splitting-validation
Coverage: reading

The reference independently assembles the SAME FD semidiscretization with a real-space sparse matrix and separately written reaction RHS, then integrates it unsplit with Radau. Tighter Radau and separate DOP853 runs measure reference sensitivity relative to the finest Strang error. Norms are per-species mean L1, RMS L2 and maximum L∞, then the worse species; refinement uses the maximum across the four common positive observation times. Also record Newton-tolerance sensitivity, positive tested substeps, reaction source/sink balance and reversed-Lie ordering.

## Operator splitting: Lie–Trotter and Strang on the same reaction–diffusion problem — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-splitting/#reaction-diffusion-splitting-limits
Coverage: reading

This measures temporal error of the adopted compositions at fixed space, including splitting and midpoint-reaction discretization errors. It is not an exact continuum solution, spatial convergence check or independent PDE-engine comparison. Reactions do not conserve u+v; positivity is observed only for the fixed input. Work is reported as actual subflow calls, without runtime rankings or universal Strang superiority. This additional comparison of the existing Schnakenberg problem changes neither physical-problem counts, the common 22 examples, old release criteria nor success history. Long-time patterns, 2D and general boundaries are outside scope.

## Operator splitting: Lie–Trotter and Strang on the same reaction–diffusion problem — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-splitting/#reaction-diffusion-splitting-references
Coverage: reading

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
H. F. Trotter (1959). On the product of semi-groups of operators · DOI: 10.1090/S0002-9939-1959-0108732-6
Review scope / review_level: metadata
AMS bibliographic record checked. Original semigroup product-limit reference; no audit of unbounded-operator hypotheses. Finite-dimensional order calculations are derived in the chapter.
G. Strang (1968). On the Construction and Comparison of Difference Schemes · DOI: 10.1137/0705041
Review scope / review_level: metadata
Publisher bibliography checked for this addition. The original symmetric splitting reference is distinct from the Hairer lecture consulted for compositions and order. No fresh full-paper audit.
E. Hairer (2010). Geometric Numerical Integration, Lecture2
Review scope / review_level: full-text
Author-hosted Lecture 2, section 5, printed pp.12–14, equations (23)–(27), and exact versus numerical subflows: Lie–Trotter, symmetric second-order composition and separable Hamiltonians. Selected passages, not a full-lecture audit.
J. Schnakenberg (1979). Simple chemical reaction systems with limit cycle behaviour · DOI: 10.1016/0022-5193(79)90042-0

## Operator splitting: Lie–Trotter and Strang on the same reaction–diffusion problem — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-splitting/#reaction-diffusion-splitting-references
Coverage: reading

Review scope / review_level: official-bibliography-and-publisher-indexed-abstract
Checked official PubMed bibliography/DOI and publisher-indexed abstract. Full text returned403. Historical source for the reaction family, not a claim to reproduce original coefficients or experiments.
The SciPy community (2024). SciPy1.14.1 solve_ivp reference
Review scope / review_level: official-versioned-documentation-selected-methods-and-tolerances
Consulted SciPy 1.14.1 methods and rtol/atol documentation. Radau order five and DOP853 order eight are independent time algorithms for the same spatial system, not exact continuum solutions.

scopeAll4preconditioned chainsets have per-observable full-prefix gates. Isotropic fixed comparator and short prefixes are reported,not required to fail or pass a mixing gate. ArviZ validates diagnostics on the immutable identical-data fixture,not on a claimed cross-platform byte-identical fresh simulation. Positive physical/mixing gates use fresh chains; analytic Gaussian moments validate joint target. Rhat/ESS/MCSE do not prove global convergence.

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
A. Vehtari et al. (2021). Rank-normalization,folding,and localization: An improved R-hat for assessing convergence of MCMC
Review scope / review_level: selected-primary-diagnostic-definitions

## Deterministic thermostats and constrained degrees of freedom — Download and execute the supplement [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostat-constraint-controls/#run-all
Coverage: reading

Run inside atlas-thermostat-constraint-controls-2026-11-25 from the ZIP. This command executes all 2 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output
Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

## Deterministic thermostats and constrained degrees of freedom — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostat-constraint-controls/#deterministic-thermostat-contrasts-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Symmetrically compose exact frozen-variable bath subflows,two subcycles per half bath. Advance eta only in E subflows and compare short trajectories against independent full extendedODE references.
\dot p=-\nabla U-\xi_1p,\quad\dot\xi_1=(2K-fT)/Q_1-\xi_2\xi_1H_{ext}=H+\sum_jQ_j\xi_j^2/2+fT\eta_1+T\sum_{j>1}\eta_j

Constraints,centre-of-mass removal and canonical statistics
These fixed linear constraints do not cover nonlinear molecular constraints,Fixman corrections or transport coefficients. Redundant systems with independent seeds need not have identical paths; CSVR dynamical correlations are empirical.

## Deterministic thermostats and constrained degrees of freedom — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostat-constraint-controls/#projected-canonical-dof-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Use three1Dparticles of masses1/2/3 in one common harmonic potential. No constraints,COM,COM-relative and a redundant-row equivalent have f3/2/1/1,each with1,024replicas.

## Deterministic thermostats and constrained degrees of freedom — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostat-constraint-controls/#projected-canonical-dof-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Apply tangent-space Langevin/CSVR in OBABO form. Build finite-time maps and noise covariance from canonical initial data; compute continuous references and stationary discrete Lyapunov solutions separately.
Cq=0,\quad CM^{-1}p=0,\quad f=3-\mathrm{rank}(C)\mathrm{Cov}(p)=T(M-C^T(CM^{-1}C^T)^+C)

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-kinetic-kernel-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Use the completed-square exact CIR transition with normal R and independent chi-square(Nf−1) S. The same R sets the sign of global alpha; S=0 for Nf=1. Reconstruct momentum from its unit direction and new radius without a tiny-K energy ratio. Reject K=0 because its direction is undefined.
\bar K=\frac{N_fT}{2},\quad c=e^{-h/\tau},\quad A=\frac{T(1-c)}2,\quad R\sim N(0,1),\ S\sim\chi^2_{N_f-1}K^\prime=(\sqrt{cK}+\sqrt A R)^2+AS,\quad \operatorname{sign}\alpha=\operatorname{sign}(\sqrt{cK}+\sqrt A R)\mathbb E[K^\prime\mid K]=cK+(1-c)\bar K,\quad\operatorname{Var}(K^\prime\mid K)=2TKc(1-c)+\frac{N_fT^2}{2}(1-c)^2K\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(N_f/2,T),\quad\operatorname{Var}(T_{\rm inst})=\frac{2T^2}{N_f},\quad C_K^{\rm bath}(t)=e^{-t/\tau}

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-kinetic-kernel-limits
Coverage: reading

A bath diagnostic, not another independent physical problem. Correct K sampling does not thermalize momentum directions by global scaling alone. The bath-only exp(−t/tau) identity is not a full-MD kinetic ACF. Statistical decisions apply to fixed seeds/budgets, not general mixing guarantees.

G. Bussi, D. Donadio and M. Parrinello (2007). Canonical sampling through velocity rescaling · DOI: 10.1063/1.2408420
Review scope / review_level: author-manuscript-selected-theory-and-appendix
Checked theory II.1–II.3 and the exact kinetic-energy propagator in Appendix A of the author manuscript arXiv:0803.4060v1 (posted 2008 for the 2007 article). The SISSA publisher PDF was unavailable. Original molecular applications are not reproduced. Direct chi-square sampling avoids copying the gamma-generation typo later noted by the author.
G. Bussi and M. Parrinello (2008). Stochastic thermostats: comparison of local and global schemes · DOI: 10.1016/j.cpc.2008.01.006
Review scope / review_level: author-manuscript-selected-equations-and-algorithm
Checked sections I–II, finite-step update Eq. (8), the sign of alpha in Eq. (9) using the same Gaussian, the Nf=1 Langevin limit and tau=1/(2 gamma). The original long Lennard-Jones transport calculations are not reproduced.
Giovanni Bussi (2026). Research algorithms: stochastic velocity rescaling
Review scope / review_level: author-official-algorithm-note

Both use exact O(h/2)–velocity-Verlet–O(h/2), or OBABO. CSVR applies one factor to all momenta; Langevin uses independent component-wise OU noise. gamma=1/(2 tau) matches bath-only K relaxation. The earlier BAOAB release is retained as a different splitting.

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/

Check canonical Gaussian/Gamma distributions and K/U/H means/variances. For finite steps, compare the Verlet-shadow position variance T/[omega²(1−h² omega²/4)] and momentum variance T against a separately constructed Lyapunov solution. Deterministic biases at h=0.2/0.1/0.05 establish second order. Check Langevin q,p,K,H correlations against independent discrete propagation; report CSVR correlations with independent-replica standard errors and tau/h dependence.

dX=1.5(.2-X)dt+.8dW,X0=.7;dimensionlessT1;8/16/32/64steps;32independent seeds×1024paths. Unbounded state,no clipping.

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-langevin-harmonic-assumptions
Coverage: reading

m=kB=T=1, omega=(1,1.7), Nf=2. tau=0.25/1, h=0.1/0.05. Evolve 8192 canonically initialized replicas and a separate 4096-replica ensemble with q,p scaled by 1.4 to t=20. Correlation lags are 0/0.5/1/2/4.

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-langevin-harmonic-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Both use exact O(h/2)–velocity-Verlet–O(h/2), or OBABO. CSVR applies one factor to all momenta; Langevin uses independent component-wise OU noise. gamma=1/(2 tau) matches bath-only K relaxation. The earlier BAOAB release is retained as a different splitting.
U(q)=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^2\omega_i^2q_i^2,\quad H=K+U,\quad\gamma=\frac1{2\tau}\Sigma_{h,i}=\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac{T}{\omega_i^2(1-h^2\omega_i^2/4)},T\right),\quad\Sigma_h=M\Sigma_hM^T+QK\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(1,T),\quad H\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(2,T),\quad\operatorname{Var}K=T^2,\quad\operatorname{Var}H=2T^2C_X(t)=\frac{\mathbb E[(X_t-\mu_X)(X_0-\mu_X)]}{\sigma_X^2},\quad\operatorname{SE}(\widehat C_X)=\frac{s_{\rm products}}{\sqrt{N_{\rm replicas}}}

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-langevin-harmonic-validation
Coverage: reading

Check canonical Gaussian/Gamma distributions and K/U/H means/variances. For finite steps, compare the Verlet-shadow position variance T/[omega²(1−h² omega²/4)] and momentum variance T against a separately constructed Lyapunov solution. Deterministic biases at h=0.2/0.1/0.05 establish second order. Check Langevin q,p,K,H correlations against independent discrete propagation; report CSVR correlations with independent-replica standard errors and tau/h dependence.

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-langevin-harmonic-limits
Coverage: reading

Global-CSVR and local-Langevin dynamical correlations are not required to agree. CDF errors are maxima over five declared points, not whole-line KS distances. Canonical-start preservation and the heated-start finite-time check do not prove ergodicity; tests retain an invariant unexcited-axis counterexample. No extrapolation to molecules, constraints or BOMD.

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-langevin-harmonic-references
Coverage: reading

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
G. Bussi, D. Donadio and M. Parrinello (2007). Canonical sampling through velocity rescaling · DOI: 10.1063/1.2408420
Review scope / review_level: author-manuscript-selected-theory-and-appendix
Checked theory II.1–II.3 and the exact kinetic-energy propagator in Appendix A of the author manuscript arXiv:0803.4060v1 (posted 2008 for the 2007 article). The SISSA publisher PDF was unavailable. Original molecular applications are not reproduced. Direct chi-square sampling avoids copying the gamma-generation typo later noted by the author.
G. Bussi and M. Parrinello (2008). Stochastic thermostats: comparison of local and global schemes · DOI: 10.1016/j.cpc.2008.01.006
Review scope / review_level: author-manuscript-selected-equations-and-algorithm

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — Anharmonic CSVR versus Langevin: distribution checks against Boltzmann quadrature [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/
Coverage: reading

Obtain coordinate normalizers/CDFs and U moments by 1D quadrature, and the H CDF by convolving exponential K with the 2D positional Boltzmann density. Save the difference between quadrature tolerances 2e−10 and 2e−12; a separate rejection ensemble also checks H. Report independent-replica standard errors for q,p,K,H correlations, keeping step differences distinct from sampling noise.

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-langevin-quartic-assumptions
Coverage: reading

m=kB=T=1, omega=(1,1.7), lambda=0.2, U=sum(omega²q²/2+lambda q⁴/4). Use 8192 canonical and 4096 heated replicas, t=20, tau=0.25/1, h=0.1/0.05, lags 0/0.5/1/2/4.

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-langevin-quartic-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Compare global CSVR and local OU with the same OBABO splitting. Draw initial canonical positions by independent Gaussian-envelope rejection and momenta from Maxwell distributions, and evolve a separate heated initial ensemble.
U(q)=\sum_{i=1}^2\left(\frac{\omega_i^2q_i^2}{2}+\frac{\lambda q_i^4}{4}\right),\quad\rho(q)=Z^{-1}e^{-U(q)/T}F_H(E)=\int_{U(q)\le E}\rho(q)\left[1-e^{-(E-U(q))/T}\right]dq,\qquad N_f=2\mathbb E H=\mathbb E K+\mathbb E U,\quad\operatorname{Var}H=\operatorname{Var}K+\operatorname{Var}U

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-langevin-quartic-validation
Coverage: reading

Obtain coordinate normalizers/CDFs and U moments by 1D quadrature, and the H CDF by convolving exponential K with the 2D positional Boltzmann density. Save the difference between quadrature tolerances 2e−10 and 2e−12; a separate rejection ensemble also checks H. Report independent-replica standard errors for q,p,K,H correlations, keeping step differences distinct from sampling noise.

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-langevin-quartic-limits
Coverage: reading

A small example for one separable two-mode quartic potential and fixed seeds. H is not treated as harmonic Gamma. No independent exact full-system dynamical reference is claimed, and neither matching correlations nor time order hidden by sampling noise is an acceptance claim. Molecular transport, quantum and ab initio MD are outside scope.

## CSVR and Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations — Primary sources and review scope [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-thermostats/#csvr-langevin-quartic-references
Coverage: reading

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
G. Bussi, D. Donadio and M. Parrinello (2007). Canonical sampling through velocity rescaling · DOI: 10.1063/1.2408420
Review scope / review_level: author-manuscript-selected-theory-and-appendix
Checked theory II.1–II.3 and the exact kinetic-energy propagator in Appendix A of the author manuscript arXiv:0803.4060v1 (posted 2008 for the 2007 article). The SISSA publisher PDF was unavailable. Original molecular applications are not reproduced. Direct chi-square sampling avoids copying the gamma-generation typo later noted by the author.
G. Bussi and M. Parrinello (2008). Stochastic thermostats: comparison of local and global schemes · DOI: 10.1016/j.cpc.2008.01.006
Review scope / review_level: author-manuscript-selected-equations-and-algorithm
Checked sections I–II, finite-step update Eq. (8), the sign of alpha in Eq. (9) using the same Gaussian, the Nf=1 Langevin limit and tau=1/(2 gamma). The original long Lennard-Jones transport calculations are not reproduced.
Giovanni Bussi (2026). Research algorithms: stochastic velocity rescaling
Review scope / review_level: author-official-algorithm-note

## Lightweight variable Eddington factor and tensor checks — Lightweight variable Eddington factor and tensor checks [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-variable-eddington-controls/
Coverage: reading

Iterate angular transport and a separate moment solve for periodic problems with a positive isotropic source, separating analytic-reference errors, balance, and spatial and angular effects.

## Lightweight variable Eddington factor and tensor checks — Download and execute the supplement [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-variable-eddington-controls/#run-all
Coverage: reading

Run inside atlas-variable-eddington-controls-2026-11-26 from the ZIP. This command executes all 2 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output
Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

## Lightweight variable Eddington factor and tensor checks — Variable Eddington factor: a periodic 1D scattering-source control [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-variable-eddington-controls/
Coverage: reading

Iteratively couple formal angular transport to independent moment equations and compare the spatially varying factor f with a closed-form reference.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Variable Eddington factor (1D VEF)
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
At each iteration solve formal Fourier transport with q+ss E_LO, extract f=Kxx/E_HO, and solve finite-difference moment equations using shared conservative faces. The primary closure never receives the analytic reference.
Static grey VEF/VET moment closure
Static steady grey unit-periodic interval; dimensionless st=4, ss=3, sa=1 and c=1. q=1+0.3 cos(2pi x), sampled as point values at x_i=i/N. Angular averages use (1/2) integral I dmu.
Problem figure
A saved validation figure for this execution example. Its conditions and acceptance scope are documented by this page’s checks.
Variable Eddington factor: a periodic 1D scattering-source control
This problem’s code and validation status
Exact / reference solutions
References and checks for this execution
Separate N=33/65 refinement at32 angular points from a64-point probe at N=65. Check analytic fields and complex modes, conservation, realizability, iteration residuals, negative controls and a separate N=9 constant-source row.

## Lightweight variable Eddington factor and tensor checks — Variable Eddington factor: a periodic 1D scattering-source control [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-variable-eddington-controls/
Coverage: reading

Same-problem reference · Analytic reference
Authored continuum Fourier response for periodic 1D VEF
The continuum-angle Fourier response to the prescribed positive isotropic source is an analytic reference for this same fixed problem. Keep point/face locations and complex phase distinct, retaining the independent HO/LO discretization gap. Position x and angular cosine mu are not two spatial dimensions. This periodic homogeneous educational control does not validate inflow boundaries, time evolution, material/fluid coupling, nonlinear FLD, general AP properties or speedup.

## Lightweight variable Eddington factor and tensor checks — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-variable-eddington-controls/#vef-fourier-scattering1d-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Static steady grey unit-periodic interval; dimensionless st=4, ss=3, sa=1 and c=1. q=1+0.3 cos(2pi x), sampled as point values at x_i=i/N. Angular averages use (1/2) integral I dmu.

## Lightweight variable Eddington factor and tensor checks — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-variable-eddington-controls/#vef-fourier-scattering1d-algorithm
Coverage: reading

At each iteration solve formal Fourier transport with q+ss E_LO, extract f=Kxx/E_HO, and solve finite-difference moment equations using shared conservative faces. The primary closure never receives the analytic reference.
\mu\partial_xI+\sigma_tI=\sigma_sE+q,\quad E=\langle I\rangle,\quad f=\langle\mu^2I\rangle/E\partial_xH+\sigma_aE=q,\quad \partial_x(fE)+\sigma_tH=0R=\frac{\arctan(k/\sigma_t)}{k},\quad A=\frac{b}{1-\sigma_sR},\quad E_{\rm ref}=1+\Re(ARe^{ikx})

Coverage: reading

Separate N=33/65 refinement at32 angular points from a64-point probe at N=65. Check analytic fields and complex modes, conservation, realizability, iteration residuals, negative controls and a separate N=9 constant-source row.

Iterate formal Fourier angular transport, D=K_HO/E_HO, and an independent finite-difference moment solve. Include both Dxy cross derivatives in shared face fluxes and check local/global discrete budgets.

## Lightweight variable Eddington factor and tensor checks — Variable Eddington tensor: a periodic 2D nonparallel-source control [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-variable-eddington-controls/
Coverage: reading

Separate17x17/33x33 refinement at12x48 angles from the16x64 angular probe on33x33. Check analytic E/H/K/D, complex modes including phase, independent angular integration, tensor constraints, cross-term negative controls and a9x9 constant source.
Same-problem reference · Analytic reference
Authored continuum Fourier response for periodic 2D VET
The continuum-angle Fourier response to the prescribed positive isotropic source is an analytic reference for this same fixed problem. Keep point/face locations and complex phase distinct, retaining the independent HO/LO discretization gap. Pointwise M1 comparison is a closure diagnostic; no M1 PDE is solved. This is not a reproduction of Athena, short characteristics, shadows, crossing beams, RHD or boundary closures, and does not claim exact fixed-grid HO/LO agreement or universal convergence rates.

## Lightweight variable Eddington factor and tensor checks — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-variable-eddington-controls/#vet-fourier-source2d-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Static steady grey unit-periodic square; dimensionless st=4, ss=3, sa=1 and c=1, using point samples. q=1+0.3 cos(2pi x)+0.2 sin(2pi(x+y)). Space is2D, but directions cover full S2 and Dzz is retained.

## Lightweight variable Eddington factor and tensor checks — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-variable-eddington-controls/#vet-fourier-source2d-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Iterate formal Fourier angular transport, D=K_HO/E_HO, and an independent finite-difference moment solve. Include both Dxy cross derivatives in shared face fluxes and check local/global discrete budgets.
\boldsymbol\Omega\cdot\nabla I+\sigma_tI=\sigma_sE+q,\quad D=\frac{\langle\boldsymbol\Omega\boldsymbol\Omega^TI\rangle}{\langle I\rangle}\sigma_t\sigma_aE-\partial_{xx}(D_{xx}E)-2\partial_{xy}(D_{xy}E)-\partial_{yy}(D_{yy}E)=\sigma_tqK_k=A\left[T\mathbb I+(C-T)\hat k\hat k^T\right],\quad C=\frac{\sigma_t(1-\sigma_tR)}{k^2},\quad T=\frac{R-C}{2}

## Nonperiodic walls: cavity and manufactured flow — Download and execute the supplement [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-wall-flow/#run-all
Coverage: reading

Run inside atlas-wall-flow-2026-11-23-r2 from the ZIP. This command executes all 2 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output
Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

## Nonperiodic walls: cavity and manufactured flow — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-wall-flow/#cavity-ghia-re100-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Dimensionless unit square, viscosity .01, lid speed1, Re=100. Top interior nodes have u=1; other walls and all four corners have zero velocity. Psi=0 on every wall; initial interior vorticity 0. Reapply Thom wall vorticity at every Heun stage.

## Nonperiodic walls: cavity and manufactured flow — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-wall-flow/#cavity-ghia-re100-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Advance vorticity transport with centered differences and Heun. Each stage solves−Delta_h psi=omega using a nonperiodic Dirichlet DST, then forms u=psi_y,v=−psi_x. Use local first-order Thom wall vorticity; this is an independent method, not Ghia CSI-MG or its higher-order wall formula.
\omega_t+u\omega_x+v\omega_y=\nu\Delta\omega,\quad -\Delta\psi=\omega,\quad (u,v)=(\psi_y,-\psi_x)\mathrm{Re}=UL/\nu=100,\quad \psi|_{\partial\Omega}=0,\quad u(x,1)=1\ (0<x<1)\omega_{\mathrm{top},i}=-2\psi_{J-1,i}/h^2-2U/h,\quad \omega_{\mathrm{stationary}}=-2\psi_{\mathrm{adj}}/h^2+O(h)\omega^{(1)}=\omega^n+\Delta t L(\omega^n),\quad \omega^{n+1}=\tfrac12\omega^n+\tfrac12[\omega^{(1)}+\Delta t L(\omega^{(1)})]

## Nonperiodic walls: cavity and manufactured flow — Nonperiodic wall MMS: velocity, shear and pressure operator [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-wall-flow/
Coverage: reading

This problem’s code and validation status
Exact / reference solutions
References and checks for this execution
Reference and validation scope
Require finest-pair psi/velocity orders ≥1.7, decreasing and bounded errors, and decreasing actual wall-vorticity/velocity-gradient shear errors. Separate pressure orders must be≥1.8 for p and≥1.7 for full/boundary gradients. Record five independent polynomial-reference checks, four-wall values, true steady residual and nonperiodic Poisson residual.
Same-problem reference · Manufactured solution
Wall manufactured solution: polynomial velocity and separate pressure operator
Thom wall vorticity has first-order local truncation; publish observed shear rates without promising second order. Pressure is eliminated from streamfunction evolution, so a pressure gauge is inapplicable. The separate operator MMS does not verify cavity pressure, traction boundaries or MAC projection. Independent polynomial differentiation is distinct from comparison with an independent flow solver.
Input and validation protocol history · Initial input

## Nonperiodic walls: cavity and manufactured flow — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-wall-flow/#wall-manufactured-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Unit square, viscosity .01,17/33/65nodes,psi8f(x)f(y), f(z)=z²(1−z)². All walls are impermeable/no-slip. Derive the curl forcing from the continuous PDE and use the same actual Thom closure as the cavity on every wall; never inject exact wall vorticity.

## Nonperiodic walls: cavity and manufactured flow — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-wall-flow/#wall-manufactured-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Use the shared centered FD/Heun/nonperiodic Dirichlet DST solver. Qualify explicit analytic derivatives against independently differentiated tensor coefficients. Separately solve nonzero-Dirichlet Poisson for p=x²+y²+sin(pi*x)sin(pi*y), checking central interior and second-order one-sided boundary gradients.
f(z)=z^2(1-z)^2,\quad \psi_\star=8f(x)f(y),\quad u_\star=\partial_y\psi_\star,\quad v_\star=-\partial_x\psi_\star,\quad\omega_\star=-\Delta\psi_\star\omega_t+u\omega_x+v\omega_y=\nu\Delta\omega+s,\quad s=u_\star\partial_x\omega_\star+v_\star\partial_y\omega_\star-\nu\Delta\omega_\starp_\star=x^2+y^2+\sin(\pi x)\sin(\pi y),\quad -\Delta p_\star=-4+2\pi^2\sin(\pi x)\sin(\pi y),\quad p|_{\partial\Omega}=p_\star\tau_{xy}/\mu=\partial_y u\quad\text{on stationary horizontal walls},\qquad p_{\mathrm{obs}}=\log_2(E_h/E_{h/2})

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-wall-flow/#wall-manufactured-references
Coverage: reading

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.
U. Ghia, K. N. Ghia and C. T. Shin (1982). High-Re solutions for incompressible flow using the Navier-Stokes equations and a multigrid method [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.1016/0021-9991(82)90058-4
Review scope / review_level: primary-original-selected-pages
Visually inspected original equations/boundary figure, Re100 columns in TablesI/II and primary vortex in TableV. The public mirror delivers the original paper; its PDF is not redistributed. This independently written solver differs from CSI-MG.
Kambiz Salari and Patrick Knupp (2000). Code Verification by the Method of Manufactured Solutions [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.2172/759450
Review scope / review_level: primary-selected-section-and-official-abstract
Read official Sandia/OSTI metadata/abstract and original report printed12 on MMS together with mesh refinement. The polynomial and pressure field are constructed for this example.

## Warm PIC: Landau damping and two-stream instability — Warm PIC linear Landau damping [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-warm-pic/
Coverage: reading

References and checks for this execution
Reference and validation scope
31pytest,19self-consistent runs,140/140case gates and17/17independent linear-reference qualifiers passed; shared pytest+main7.283s. Landau256/512particle-space curve gap.001154 and amplitude-half gap.004376 meet the unchanged.03bound. Original64-strata130/131result (.05646>.03) remains an explicitly unmet retained example; amplitudes/all tolerances stayed fixed.
Same-problem reference · Semi-analytic reference
Warm PIC linear Landau damping
Small fixed1D1V collisionless electrons with fixed ions. Every positive-weight Gauss-velocity full-f carrier moves. Seed SE/t intervals are conditional on quiet spatial shifts, not iid particle noise or N^(-1/2) convergence. Velocity-quadrature bias has a separate doubling probe. The independent reference is a derived linear continuum IVP, not a second nonlinear Vlasov engine. Late two-stream behavior is diagnostic; no saturation-value gate. Even-grid Nyquist charge is separately reported rather than included in a full-spectrum Gauss claim. Four-shift Student-t intervals are nominal conditional summaries; neither coverage of the exact rate nor total error is established.

## Warm PIC: Landau damping and two-stream instability — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-warm-pic/#thermal-landau-damping-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Positive Gaussian velocity weights and density-CDF inversion load the joint(x,v) distribution. Recompute CIC deposition, FFT Poisson and matched CIC gathering at every velocity-Verlet kick. Qualify the dielectric root using branch continuation/bracket checks and a separately derived, time-refined Volterra IVP with the same fixed-window estimator.
\partial_t f+v\partial_x f-E\partial_v f=0,\quad\partial_x E=1-\int f\,dv,\quad\langle E\rangle=0D(\omega,k)=1+\frac{1}{k^2}\sum_s a_s[1+\zeta_s Z(\zeta_s)],\quad\zeta_s=\frac{\omega-ku_s}{\sqrt2 k}e(t)=\Phi(t)-\int_0^t s\Phi(s)e(t-s)\,ds,\quad\Phi(t)=e^{-k^2t^2/2}\cos(kut)

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-warm-pic/
Coverage: reading

31pytest,19self-consistent runs,140/140case gates and17/17independent linear-reference qualifiers passed; shared pytest+main7.283s. Same-problem reference · Semi-analytic reference
Warm PIC two-stream initial growth
Small fixed1D1V collisionless electrons with fixed ions. Every positive-weight Gauss-velocity full-f carrier moves. Seed SE/t intervals are conditional on quiet spatial shifts, not iid particle noise or N^(-1/2) convergence. Velocity-quadrature bias has a separate doubling probe. The independent reference is a derived linear continuum IVP, not a second nonlinear Vlasov engine. Late two-stream behavior is diagnostic; no saturation-value gate. Even-grid Nyquist charge is separately reported rather than included in a full-spectrum Gauss claim. Four-shift Student-t intervals are nominal conditional summaries; neither coverage of the exact rate nor total error is established.

## Warm PIC: Landau damping and two-stream instability — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-warm-pic/#thermal-two-stream-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Positive Gaussian velocity weights and density-CDF inversion load the joint(x,v) distribution. Recompute CIC deposition, FFT Poisson and matched CIC gathering at every velocity-Verlet kick. Qualify the dielectric root using branch continuation/bracket checks and a separately derived, time-refined Volterra IVP with the same fixed-window estimator.
\partial_t f+v\partial_x f-E\partial_v f=0,\quad\partial_x E=1-\int f\,dv,\quad\langle E\rangle=0D(\omega,k)=1+\frac{1}{k^2}\sum_s a_s[1+\zeta_s Z(\zeta_s)],\quad\zeta_s=\frac{\omega-ku_s}{\sqrt2 k}e(t)=\Phi(t)-\int_0^t s\Phi(s)e(t-s)\,ds,\quad\Phi(t)=e^{-k^2t^2/2}\cos(kut)

## WENO critical points and epsilon dependence — WENO critical points and epsilon dependence [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-weno-critical/
Coverage: reading

Compare critical-point reconstruction from cell means using WENO-JS/Z power-two weights and actual periodic scalar transport. Separate epsilon choices, analytic cell means versus point values, and spatial error versus time-step effects. For the selected first-critical polynomial, both tiny-epsilon JS and Z show local rates about5; Z has a smaller leading error.

## WENO critical points and epsilon dependence — Download and execute the supplement [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-weno-critical/#run-all
Coverage: reading

Run inside atlas-weno-critical-2026-11-23 from the ZIP. This command executes all 1 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output
Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

## WENO critical points and epsilon dependence — WENO-JS/Z: fixed critical-point and epsilon comparison [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-weno-critical/
Coverage: reading

Pre-run contract fixes72 local reconstructions,24 PDE runs and36 pytest checks. Qualify analytic means against independent Gauss12 quadrature; retain local errors/weights, transport L1/L2/Linf, mass, stage finiteness, intermediate times and shared-flux budgets. Six finest-grid half-dt differences must be at most10% of corresponding continuum errors.
Related-model reference · Analytic reference
Advection / sine translation
Same periodic sine-transport model at speed one. The library amplitude is 0.25 versus 0.2 in the common fixed input; DG/CIP representations and output times also differ.
Related-model reference · Analytic reference
WENO critical points: polynomial cell means and analytic periodic transport
An additional constant-speed periodic-transport reference. The cos+.1sin³ cell means and local critical polynomials differ from the historical single-sine/CIP display.
Same-problem reference · Analytic reference
FR/DG periodic sine advection: analytic reference at mean0.4 andT=.25
Dimensionless u_t+u_x=0 on[0,1), periodic boundary, initial0.4+sin(2pi x), analytic0.4+sin(2pi(x-t)). Constant positive speed1 and uniform affine intervals.

## WENO critical points and epsilon dependence — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-weno-critical/#weno-critical-epsilon-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Local polynomials have center x=0 and target h/2, h=1/64…1/512. Transport uses periodic[0,1], unit speed, q₀=cos(2πx)+.1sin³(2πx), T=1 and32/64/128 cells. All evolved states/references are FV cell means, not point samples.

## WENO critical points and epsilon dependence — Adopted numerical method [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-weno-critical/#weno-critical-epsilon-algorithm
Coverage: reading

Share three candidates, linear weights(.1,.6,.3) and JS indicators. Normalize JS d/(beta+epsilon)² or Z d[1+(|beta0−beta2|/(beta+epsilon))²]. Use epsilon10⁻⁴⁰,10⁻⁶,h². Actual transport uses shared upwind face fluxes and classical RK4 at Courant.1 without state clipping/retries.
\bar q_i=h^{-1}\int_{x_i-h/2}^{x_i+h/2}q(x)\,dx,\qquad q^-_{i+1/2}=\sum_{k=0}^2\omega_k p_k(p_0,p_1,p_2)=\frac16(2\bar q_{i-2}-7\bar q_{i-1}+11\bar q_i,-\bar q_{i-1}+5\bar q_i+2\bar q_{i+1},2\bar q_i+5\bar q_{i+1}-\bar q_{i+2})\omega_k=\alpha_k/\sum_j\alpha_j,\quad d=(.1,.6,.3),\quad\alpha_k^{JS}=d_k/(\epsilon+\beta_k)^2,\quad\alpha_k^Z=d_k[1+(\tau_5/(\epsilon+\beta_k))^2],\quad\tau_5=|\beta_0-\beta_2|\partial_tq+\partial_xq=0,\quad q(x,t)=q_0(x-t),\quad\frac{d\bar q_i}{dt}=-\frac{q^-_{i+1/2}-q^-_{i-1/2}}h\bar q_i(t)=\operatorname{sinc}(h)\cos\theta_i+.075\operatorname{sinc}(h)\sin\theta_i-.025\operatorname{sinc}(3h)\sin(3\theta_i),\quad\theta_i=2\pi(x_i-t),\quad\operatorname{sinc}(z)=\frac{\sin\pi z}{\pi z}

## WENO critical points and epsilon dependence — References and measured quantities [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-weno-critical/#weno-critical-epsilon-validation
Coverage: reading

Pre-run contract fixes72 local reconstructions,24 PDE runs and36 pytest checks. ## WENO critical points and epsilon dependence — Verification limits and failures [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-weno-critical/#weno-critical-epsilon-limits
Coverage: reading

Order gates concern the chosen first-critical interface reconstruction; second-critical values remain diagnostic. Fixed epsilon depends on amplitude/units. Distinguish reconstruction order from PDE convergence and this FV implementation from original FD papers. No shock/Euler/MHD, arbitrary higher-critical-point, universal stability/TVD or positivity guarantee is claimed.

## Zalesak-type 2D rotation: conservation, bounds and shape error — Zalesak-type 2D rotation: conservation, bounds and shape error [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-zalesak/
Coverage: reading

A two-dimensional scalar conservation law transports a slotted disk in a prescribed rigid-rotation velocity. Compare donor-cell upwinding and minmod MUSCL with the same SSPRK(3,3), checking full-turn mass, bounds, shape error and dependence on grid placement and initial angle. The base refinements use64²,128² and256² cells, with separate placement and initial-angle diagnostics at64².

## Zalesak-type 2D rotation: conservation, bounds and shape error — Zalesak-type 2D rotation: conservation, bounds and shape error [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-zalesak/
Coverage: reading

Rotate a slotted disk through one full turn with an actual 2D finite-volume solver, comparing donor-cell and minmod MUSCL. Eight runs combine three grids with half-cell-center and 45-degree-start probes; measure conservation, bounds at every SSP stage, shape error and slot filling.
Methods, equations, figures and references
Methods used
Upwind finite differences
MUSCL reconstruction
Minmod
SSPRK(3,3)
Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.
Equations
This example’s formulation and conditions
Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope
Use analytic divergence-free normal face averages and one shared upwind flux per interface. Both piecewise-constant donor-cell and mean-preserving directional-minmod MUSCL use SSPRK(3,3). The four face-midpoint mean equals the cell mean; individual outgoing-face Courant<=1/4 gives a convex FE update. Check the actual .20 bound at every stage. No transported-state clipping/floors or rejected/retried steps are used.
Two-dimensional rotational advection
Two-dimensional conservative transport of q with prescribed a=-omega(y-yc), b=omega(x-xc), whose divergence is zero. Shared face velocities and numerical fluxes update scalar cell means.
Problem figure
A saved validation figure for this execution example. Its conditions and acceptance scope are documented by this page’s checks.

## Zalesak-type 2D rotation: conservation, bounds and shape error — Assumptions, units and boundaries [en]

Source: https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/en/read/validation-zalesak/#zalesak-rotation-assumptions
Coverage: reading

Fix the dimensionless unit square, rotation center(.5,.5), disk center(.5,.75), radius.15, slot width.05/top y=.85, angular speed1, T=2pi and64²/128²/256² cells. The body is1 and exterior/slot0. Periodic normal face velocities match; the exact compact support stays away from the boundary.
